questions.explanation:
Governing principle: hardness from bicarbonates (hydrogen trioxocarbonate (IV)) of Ca2+ is temporary because these salts decompose on heating.
Decomposition on heating: Ca(HCO3)2 → CaCO3(s) ↓ + CO2(g) + H2O, so Ca2+ is removed as insoluble CaCO3.
Because the dissolved Ca(HCO3)2 can be precipitated and removed by boiling, the hardness it causes is removable.
Correct answer: B. Temporary hardness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: Which gas law states that the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature at constant volume?
questions.explanation:
Pressure Law (Gay-Lussac's Law) states that for a fixed mass of gas at constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature.
Using the ideal gas law PV = nRT with V and n constant gives P = (nR/V)·T, so P ∝ T.
This direct proportionality of pressure with temperature at constant volume is the core of the Pressure Law.
Therefore the correct option is C: Pressure Law (Gay-Lussac's Law).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Acid hydrolysis of sucrose (cane sugar) yields an equimolar mixture of
questions.explanation:
Acid hydrolysis cleaves the glycosidic bond of a disaccharide to yield its component monosaccharides in equimolar amounts.
Sucrose is composed of one glucose and one fructose unit joined by an α,β-1,2-glycosidic bond.
Acidic hydrolysis breaks this bond to give one glucose and one fructose per sucrose molecule.
Therefore the products are an equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose, so option B is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which indicator turns pink/magenta in alkaline solutions and remains colorless in acidic solutions?
questions.explanation:
Acid–base indicators change color by protonation/deprotonation at characteristic pH values.
Phenolphthalein is colorless in acidic or neutral solution and turns pink/magenta in alkaline solution (around pH 8.2–10).
Methyl orange, litmus and bromothymol blue have different color changes and so do not match the described behavior.
Therefore the correct choice is C. Phenolphthalein.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Pure alumina (Al2O3) is dissolved in molten cryolite (Na3AlF6) during aluminum extraction to
options: lower the melting point of alumina
increase the purity of aluminum metal
questions.explanation:
Principle: electrolysis requires a molten electrolyte and lowering the melting point reduces operating temperature and energy demand.
Cryolite acts as a solvent/flux in which Al2O3 dissolves, producing a molten mixture with a much lower melting point than pure alumina.
The resulting molten electrolyte also has sufficient ionic conductivity for efficient aluminium extraction at practical temperatures.
Hence option B is correct — cryolite is used primarily to lower the melting point of alumina.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many carbon-carbon double bonds are formally represented in a Kekulé structure of benzene (C6H6)?
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: The Kekulé structure of benzene is shown as a six-membered ring with alternating single and double C–C bonds.
Alternation means every other bond around the ring is a double bond.
Counting those gives 6 ÷ 2 = 3 carbon–carbon double bonds.
Correct option: C (3).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An aqueous solution turns red litmus paper blue and records a pH of 11. The solution contains an excess of
questions.explanation:
pH > 7 indicates a basic solution where OH- concentration exceeds H+ (Kw = 1.0×10^-14).
Red litmus turning blue confirms the solution is basic.
pH 11 gives [H+] = 10^-11 M.
[OH-] = Kw/[H+] = 1.0×10^-14 / 10^-11 = 10^-3 M.
Since OH- (10^-3 M) > H+ (10^-11 M), the solution contains an excess of OH- (option B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which element is located in Period 3, Group 1 of the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: Period number equals the highest occupied shell and Group 1 elements have one valence electron (alkali metals).
Period 3 therefore has highest shell n=3, and a Group 1 element will have an outer electron in 3s.
Sodium has electronic configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1, so it is an n=3 element with one valence electron.
Hence the element in Period 3, Group 1 is Sodium — Option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The subatomic particle possessing a unit positive charge and a relative atomic mass of 1 amu is a
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: protons carry a unit positive charge (+1) and have a relative mass of about 1 atomic mass unit (1 amu), while electrons are −1 and neutrons are neutral.
The description “unit positive charge and relative mass 1 amu” matches the proton.
Therefore the correct option is B (Proton).
Electrons are negatively charged, neutrons have no charge, and alpha particles have +2 charge and ~4 amu, so they are incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which organic functional group reduces Fehling's solution to yield a brick-red precipitate of copper (I) oxide?
questions.explanation:
Fehling's solution oxidizes aldehydes to carboxylic acids while reducing Cu2+ to brick-red Cu2O.
The aldehyde functional group (–CHO) is easily oxidized under these conditions, unlike ketones, alcohols or acids.
An alkanal contains the –CHO group, so it will reduce Fehling's to give the brick-red copper(I) oxide precipitate.
Therefore the correct option is B: Alkanal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The industrial process of coating iron sheet surfaces with thin tin metal to prevent corrosion is known as
questions.explanation:
Principle: Corrosion is prevented by a continuous metal coating that blocks oxygen/water and/or provides electrochemical protection; electroplating deposits such a coating.
In tinning, tin ions are reduced onto the iron surface by electrolysis to form a thin protective tin layer.
Galvanizing refers specifically to zinc coating; vulcanization is for rubber and annealing is a heat treatment, so they are incorrect.
Therefore coating iron sheets with thin tin metal is called electroplating/tinning (Option B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Iron is often galvanized in order to
questions.explanation:
Principle: galvanizing applies a zinc coating that forms a physical barrier and gives sacrificial protection because zinc is more reactive than iron.
Reasoning: the zinc layer prevents moisture and oxygen from contacting the iron and corrodes preferentially.
Result: the underlying iron is thereby kept from rusting (corroding).
Therefore this matches option C: protect it against corrosion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the industrial production of hydrogen gas, carbon (II) oxide (CO) is removed from the reaction mixture by
questions.explanation:
Principle: selective chemical absorption—CO is removed by complexation with Cu(I) in an ammoniacal solution while H2 is inert.
Reason: CO forms a stable soluble complex with cuprous chloride in ammonia, so CO is retained and removed from the gas stream.
Other options fail: limewater removes CO2, P2O5 only dries gases, and water washing does not selectively absorb CO.
Therefore passing the mixture through ammoniacal copper(I) chloride solution (option D) removes CO.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The gas that is most useful in protecting humans against solar radiation is
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: a protective atmospheric gas must strongly absorb harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun.
Ozone (O3) in the stratosphere absorbs most UV-B and UV-C, preventing these high-energy rays from reaching Earth's surface.
Chlorine, carbon (IV) oxide (CO2) and hydrogen sulfide do not significantly absorb these UV bands and so provide little protection.
Therefore the gas most useful in protecting humans against solar radiation is ozone — option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Vulcanization of natural rubber involves the reaction/removal of
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: Vulcanization uses sulfur to form cross-links in polyisoprene by reacting at carbon–carbon double bonds.
Key reasoning: Sulfur atoms add to or bridge the C=C sites, converting those double bonds into sulfur-linked single bonds between chains.
This cross-linking therefore consumes or alters the double bonds and stabilizes the rubber’s mechanical properties.
Conclusion: Vulcanization involves reaction/removal of double bonds, so option C is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The acid used to acidify water in the electrolysis of water is dilute
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: electrolysis of water needs high ionic conductivity and anions that will not be oxidized at the anode.
A strong acid increases H+ concentration and conductivity; CH3COOH is weak and gives poor conductivity.
HCl supplies Cl− which is oxidized to Cl2 at the anode (undesirable), whereas H2SO4 supplies H+ and relatively inert SO4^2−.
Therefore dilute H2SO4 (option C) is used to acidify water for electrolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When a salt loses its water of crystallization to the atmosphere on exposure, the process is called
questions.explanation:
Hydrated salts contain water of crystallization that can be lost or gained depending on vapor pressure differences with the atmosphere.
If the vapor pressure of the water in the crystal exceeds the surrounding atmospheric vapor pressure, the salt releases that water and becomes less hydrated.
The process of losing water of crystallization on exposure is called efflorescence.
Deliquescence is the opposite (absorption of moisture), effervescence is gas evolution and fluorescence is light emission, so option A is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The atomicity of ozone is
questions.explanation:
Atomicity is the number of atoms present in a single molecule of a substance.
Ozone has the molecular formula O3, indicating one molecule contains three oxygen atoms.
Thus a single ozone molecule contains three atoms.
Therefore the atomicity of ozone is 3, matching option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the noble gases has the greatest ionization energy?
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: ionization energy increases across a period and up a group because smaller atoms hold their electrons more tightly.
Among noble gases the highest ionization energy will be for the smallest, topmost atom in the group.
Helium has the smallest atomic radius and highest effective nuclear attraction per electron, so it requires the most energy to remove an electron.
Correct answer: A. He

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cathode rays cause an object placed behind a perforated anode to cast a sharp shadow on a screen. This observation shows that cathode rays
questions.explanation:
Principle: A sharp shadow is produced only when the illuminating rays travel in straight lines from the source through apertures.
In the cathode ray setup the rays that pass the perforated anode reach the screen while the object blocks those straight paths, producing a clear outline.
If the rays were bent, scattered or widely diverging the shadow edges would be blurred rather than sharp.
Therefore the observation shows cathode rays travel in straight lines, which is option D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Flow of electric current in electrolytes is due to the movement of
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: in electrolytes, conduction occurs by migration of charged species (charged particles) under an applied electric field.
Key reasoning: when a potential is applied, cations move toward the cathode and anions toward the anode, carrying charge through the medium.
Electrons do not travel through the bulk of the electrolyte; electron transfer happens only at the electrodes while ions move through the solution.
Therefore the flow of electric current in electrolytes is due to ions — option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A suitable reagent to distinguish between ethanoic acid and ethanol is
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: carboxylic acids react with carbonates/bicarbonates to produce carbon dioxide gas, whereas alcohols do not.
Reaction: CH3COOH + NaHCO3 → CH3COONa + CO2↑ + H2O, showing CO2 evolution with ethanoic acid.
Key reasoning: ethanol has no acidic proton to liberate CO2 from bicarbonate, so no effervescence occurs.
Therefore sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate (IV) (option C) is the suitable reagent to distinguish them.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An electronic configuration of 1s2 2s2 2p3 represents the atom of
questions.explanation:
Principle: for a neutral atom, the electron configuration's total electrons equals the atomic number.
1s2 2s2 2p3 → 2+2+3 = 7 electrons.
Atomic number 7 identifies nitrogen.
Therefore the configuration represents nitrogen, option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following metals burns with a characteristic brick-red flame?
questions.explanation:
Flame tests rely on metal ions emitting characteristic colors when their electrons are excited by heat and then relax, producing visible emission.
Sodium gives an intense yellow flame, magnesium burns with a bright white flame, and lead shows no distinctive brick‑red emission.
Calcium ions produce a brick‑red (orange‑red) flame in flame tests, which matches the question's description.
Therefore the correct option is B (Ca).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A non-polar liquid suitable for dissolving fats and oils is
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: like dissolves like — non‑polar solvents dissolve non‑polar solutes.
Fats and oils are non‑polar substances, so they dissolve in non‑polar solvents.
HCl, calcium hydroxide solution and water are polar (aqueous) and do not dissolve fats, while kerosene is non‑polar.
Therefore kerosene (option C) is the suitable non‑polar liquid for dissolving fats and oils.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Tartaric acid is used industrially to
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: an acid reacts with sodium bicarbonate in baking powder to release CO2 gas that leavens dough.
Tartaric acid supplies the H+ needed to react with NaHCO3 in this acid–base reaction.
NaHCO3 + H+ → Na+ + CO2↑ + H2O (CO2 gas causes rising).
Therefore tartaric acid is used industrially as the acidic component in baking powder (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hydrogen gas can be displaced from a hot concentrated alkaline solution by
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: a metal that is more reactive than hydrogen and amphoteric will dissolve in hot concentrated alkali, forming a soluble complex and releasing H2.
Zinc is amphoteric and reacts with NaOH: Zn + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 + H2, showing displacement of hydrogen.
Copper is not reactive enough and does not displace H2; iron is not amphoteric under these conditions.
Therefore zinc (option C) displaces hydrogen from a hot concentrated alkaline solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following types of alkanols undergo oxidation to produce alkanoic acids? I. Primary alkanols II. Secondary alkanols III. Tertiary alkanols
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: primary alkanols oxidize to aldehydes and further to alkanoic acids, secondary alkanols oxidize to ketones, and tertiary alkanols resist oxidation without C–C bond cleavage.
Key reasoning: formation of a carboxyl group requires a hydrogen on the carbon bearing the OH, which only primary alkanols have.
Secondary alkanols lack that hydrogen so give ketones and do not form acids under normal oxidation; tertiary alkanols are generally resistant.
Therefore only primary alkanols produce alkanoic acids — option D (I only).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A major source of oxides of nitrogen in the atmosphere is the combustion of
options: fossil fuels in internal combustion engines
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: At the high temperatures of combustion, atmospheric nitrogen reacts with oxygen to form oxides of nitrogen (NOx).
Key reasoning: Internal-combustion engines burn fossil fuels under high temperature and pressure with abundant air, producing large amounts of NOx.
Coal and wood also emit some NOx, while chlorofluorocarbons do not produce NOx.
Therefore the major source among the options is fossil fuels in internal combustion engines — option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following substances is commonly used as a nuclear fuel?
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: nuclear fuels are elements with isotopes capable of sustaining a fission chain reaction (fissile isotopes).
Key reasoning: uranium contains the fissile isotope U-235 and is the primary fuel loaded into most commercial reactors.
Comparison: palladium is not a reactor fuel, actinium is not used as a common reactor fuel, and thorium, though a possible candidate, is not commonly used today.
Therefore the correct choice is A. Uranium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The aqueous leachate of plant ash is useful in local soap making because it contains
options: soluble carbonates and hydroxides of potassium
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: saponification requires an alkali (hydroxide or carbonate) to hydrolyse fats into soap.
Plant ash leachate dissolves potassium-rich salts, producing soluble potassium carbonates and hydroxides when leached with water.
These dissolved K2CO3 and KOH provide the alkaline medium needed for local soap making.
Therefore the correct option is D: soluble carbonates and hydroxides of potassium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction Cu2S(s) + O2(g) -> 2Cu(s) + SO2(g), the oxidation state of copper changes from
questions.explanation:
Use oxidation-state rules: sulfur in sulfides is −2 and elemental copper is 0.
In Cu2S, 2×(Ox. state of Cu) + (−2) = 0 → 2Cu = +2 → Cu = +1.
In the products Cu(s) is elemental copper, so its oxidation state is 0.
Thus copper changes from +1 to 0, which matches option A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The calorific (energy) value of fuel like petrol can be determined using a
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: calorific value is the heat released by complete combustion of a known mass of fuel, measured with a calorimeter of known heat capacity.
A bomb calorimeter burns the fuel in oxygen in a sealed vessel and measures the temperature rise of the surrounding water/calorimeter to compute energy per gram.
This direct measurement of combustion heat makes the bomb calorimeter the correct method to determine petrol's energy value (Option A).
Catalytic crackers and fractionating columns are refinery units, and a thermometer alone cannot measure the total heat released by combustion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen, and 53.3% oxygen. If its molar mass is 180 g/mol, find its molecular formula. [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation:
Use percent composition to find the empirical formula: assume 100 g → C 40.0 g, H 6.7 g, O 53.3 g.
Moles: C 40/12 = 3.333, H 6.7/1 = 6.700, O 53.3/16 = 3.331; divide by smallest (≈3.331) → C:1.00 H:2.01 O:1.00 ≈ CH2O.
Empirical molar mass = 12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30 g·mol−1.
Molecular mass 180/30 = 6 → molecular formula (CH2O)6 = C6H12O6, so option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The oxidation state of chromium in potassium heptaoxodichromate (VI), K2Cr2O7, is
questions.explanation:
Use the rule that the sum of oxidation states in a neutral compound equals zero.
K is +1, O is −2, so 2(+1)+2(Cr)+7(−2)=0.
2+2x−14=0 → 2x−12=0 → x=+6.
Therefore the oxidation state of Cr is +6, corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which group of elements belongs to the third period of the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation:
Principle: elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells equal to the period number.
Third-period elements have atomic numbers 11–18: Na(11), Mg(12), Al(13), Si(14), P(15), S(16), Cl(17), Ar(18).
Option D lists Na, Mg, S, Ar, which are all within atomic numbers 11–18 and therefore in period 3.
Therefore D is the correct choice.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Detergents manufactured with straight hydrocarbon chains are preferred because they are
questions.explanation:
Molecular structure controls biodegradability; straight hydrocarbon chains are more accessible to microbial enzymes than branched chains.
Enzymes can oxidize and cleave linear chains stepwise, whereas branching sterically hinders enzymatic attack.
Therefore detergents with straight chains are decomposed more readily in the environment.
This directly explains why option B (biodegradable) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following air pollutants directly leads to the formation of acid rain?
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: acid rain results when acidic oxides in air react with water to form strong acids.
Key reactions: sulfur oxides (SO2, SO3) form sulfuric acid (H2SO4) and nitrogen oxides (NO, NO2) form nitric acid (HNO3) after oxidation and dissolution.
Other pollutants like lead oxides, particulate matter, and hydrocarbons do not directly produce these soluble acids.
Thus the correct answer is C: oxides of sulfur and nitrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: A characteristic feature of a chemical change compared to a physical change is that
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: a chemical change alters chemical composition to produce substances with new chemical properties.
Key reasoning: this involves breaking and forming chemical bonds, whereas physical changes only alter state, shape, or arrangement without creating new substances.
Connection to correct option: therefore the distinguishing feature is that a new substance is formed (option D).
Why not the others: oxygen consumption, heat flow, or reversibility are not universal criteria for chemical change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the equilibrium PCl5(g) <=> PCl3(g) + Cl2(g), a decrease in pressure will
questions.explanation:
Le Chatelier's principle: a decrease in pressure shifts an equilibrium toward the side with more gas moles.
For PCl5(g) ⇌ PCl3(g) + Cl2(g) there is 1 mole of gas on the left and 2 moles on the right.
Lowering pressure therefore shifts the equilibrium to the right, producing more PCl3 and Cl2.
Hence the yield of PCl3 increases (Option B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds forms a precipitate when treated with aqueous NaOH solution?
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: OH− precipitates cations that form insoluble hydroxides.
Al3+ + 3OH− → Al(OH)3(s), which is insoluble, so AlCl3 gives a precipitate.
NH4+ is converted to NH3 (soluble) by OH−, and Na+ salts (Na2CO3, CH3COONa) stay soluble.
Hence only AlCl3 (option A) produces a precipitate with aqueous NaOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The electronic configuration of an element with atomic number 13 (13X) in sub-shells is
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: electrons fill subshells by increasing energy (Aufbau) with capacities 1s2, 2s2, 2p6, 3s2, 3p6.
13 electrons → fill 1s2 (2), 2s2 (4), 2p6 (10); 3 electrons remain.
Place remaining: 3s2 (12), 3p1 (13) giving 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1.
This configuration matches option A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What volume of oxygen gas at S.T.P. is required for complete combustion of 45 cm3 of methane gas (CH4)?
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: at the same T and P gas volumes are proportional to mole ratios from the balanced equation.
Balanced equation: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O.
Thus 1 volume CH4 requires 2 volumes O2, so 45 cm3 CH4 × 2 = 90 cm3 O2.
Required volume = 90.0 cm3, which corresponds to option D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The element used in the steel industry to oxidize carbon, sulfur, and phosphorus impurities from pig iron is
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: impurities in pig iron are removed by oxidation, converting them to volatile gases or oxides.
Oxygen is a strong oxidizing agent that converts carbon to CO/CO2, sulfur to SO2 and phosphorus to P2O5.
In the steel industry oxygen is blown through molten pig iron (basic oxygen process) to oxidize and remove these impurities.
Therefore the correct choice is A: oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When glucose is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4), it is dehydrated to leave a solid black residue of
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: concentrated H2SO4 acts as a strong dehydrating agent and removes water from sugars.
Key reasoning: glucose C6H12O6 is dehydrated to give elemental carbon plus water (e.g. C6H12O6 → 6C + 6H2O), producing a charred black solid.
This black residue is elemental carbon (char), not CO2, ethane, or ethanol.
Therefore the correct choice is A (carbon).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which organic compound is represented by the molecular formula C2H6O?
questions.explanation:
Principle: match the given molecular formula to known organic functional groups and molecular formulas.
Ethanol is C2H5OH, which simplifies to C2H6O, so it fits the formula.
Propanal is C3H6O, methanoic acid is HCOOH (CH2O2), and glucose is C6H12O6, so they do not match C2H6O.
Therefore the correct option is B: Ethanol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the pH of a 0.001 mol/dm3 solution of sodium hydroxide (NaOH)?
questions.explanation:
Use pOH = -log[OH-] and pH + pOH = 14.
NaOH is a strong base so [OH-] = 0.001 mol/dm3 = 1.0×10^-3 M.
pOH = -log(1.0×10^-3) = 3.
pH = 14 − 3 = 11, so option D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the endothermic gaseous reaction N2O4(g) <=> 2NO2(g), the yield of product (NO2) is favored by
questions.explanation:
Le Chatelier's principle: a change in pressure shifts a gaseous equilibrium to oppose the change.
For N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g) the number of gas moles increases from 1 to 2 (Δn = +1), so products have more moles.
Lowering the pressure favors the side with more gas molecules, shifting equilibrium to the right and increasing NO2 yield.
Therefore the yield of NO2 is favored by a decrease in pressure (option C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine gas turns damp starch-iodide paper
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: chlorine is a strong oxidizing agent and oxidizes iodide ions to iodine.
Key reaction: Cl2 + 2 I^- → 2 Cl^- + I2.
Iodine produced reacts with starch to give the characteristic dark blue starch–iodine complex on the damp paper.
Therefore the correct answer is D: dark blue.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine consists of two isotopes, mass 35 and 37. If its relative atomic mass is 35.5, calculate the percentage abundance of the isotope with mass number 37.
questions.explanation:
The relative atomic mass is the weighted average: 35*(1−x)+37*x=35.5 where x is the fraction of 37Cl.
Expand: 35 + 2x = 35.5.
Solve: 2x = 0.5 → x = 0.25.
Thus the percentage abundance of 37Cl is 25%, so option B is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The principal constituent of natural gas is
questions.explanation:
Natural gas is a mixture of light alkanes and the principal constituent is the simplest alkane produced by decomposition of organic matter.
Methane (CH4) is the lightest alkane, formed in greatest abundance under gas-forming conditions and remains gaseous at reservoir conditions.
These factors make methane the dominant component of natural gas, often comprising the majority of its volume.
Therefore the correct choice is A: methane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: One mole of a hydrocarbon contains 36 g of carbon and has a vapor density of 20. What is its structural formula?
questions.explanation:
Vapor density = molar mass/2, so M = 2×20 = 40 g mol⁻¹.
Carbon mass 36 g → 36/12 = 3 C atoms; remaining mass 4 g → 4 H atoms, giving formula C3H4.
C3H4 requires a triple bond (propyne) to satisfy valency, which matches CH3C≡CH.
Therefore the correct option is A. CH3C≡CH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the electrolysis of aqueous CuSO4 solution using platinum electrodes, the reaction occurring at the anode is
questions.explanation:
Oxidation occurs at the anode and with inert platinum the sulfate ion is not oxidized, so water/hydroxide is oxidized instead.
Hydroxide produced from water at the anode is more easily oxidized than SO4^2-, leading to O2 evolution.
Balanced anode half‑reaction: 4OH- - 4e- -> 2H2O + O2.
This equation corresponds to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The s-block elements of the Periodic Table are made up of
questions.explanation:
Governing principle: s-block elements are those whose valence electrons occupy an s orbital.
Key reasoning: Group 1 elements have valence configuration ns^1 and Group 2 have ns^2, so both fill the s subshell.
Groups beyond 2 have valence electrons in p or d orbitals, so they are not part of the s-block.
Therefore the s-block consists of Groups 1 and 2, which corresponds to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The oxidation state of oxygen in tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid (H2SO4) is
questions.explanation:
Use the rule that the sum of oxidation states equals the molecule's charge; sulfur is +6 in tetraoxosulphate(VI).
For H2SO4: 2(+1) + (+6) + 4(x) = 0.
So 2 + 6 + 4x = 0 → 8 + 4x = 0 → x = -2.
Therefore the oxidation state of oxygen is -2, which is option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the industrial electrolysis of brine, the anode material used is
questions.explanation:
Principle: the anode in brine electrolysis must be inert and corrosion-resistant so it does not oxidize or contaminate products while chloride is discharged.
At the anode Cl− is oxidized to Cl2, creating a strongly oxidizing environment that would dissolve reactive metals like Cu or Zn.
Although Pt is chemically inert, it is impractical industrially; carbon (graphite) and titanium are inert and resist chlorine attack.
Therefore the correct choice is D: carbon / titanium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following characterizes a mature plant cell?
options: A. the cytoplasm fills up the entire cell space
B. the nucleus is pushed to the centre of the cell
C. the cell wall is made up of cellulose
D. the nucleus is small and irregular in shape
questions.explanation:
Concept: features of a mature plant cell — a rigid cell wall, a large central vacuole, cytoplasm distribution, and nucleus position.
C is correct because mature plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose that provides structural support.
Reject B (nucleus central): in mature plant cells the large central vacuole pushes the nucleus toward the cell periphery rather than placing it in the centre.
Exam takeaway: pick the option stating a cellulose cell wall and eliminate choices that say the cytoplasm fills the whole cell or that the nucleus is centrally located.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the nucleus of a cell?
options: A. it controls the life processes of the cell
B. it translates genetic information for the manufacture of proteins
C. it stores and carries hereditary information
D. it is reservoir of energy for the cell
questions.explanation:
Concept: the nucleus is the cell's control center that stores hereditary information and directs protein synthesis.
Why D is correct: the nucleus does not act as an energy reservoir—energy production and storage are functions of organelles like mitochondria, which produce ATP.
Reject the closest misconception: option B's phrase 'translates genetic information' is misleading because the nucleus directs and supplies genetic templates but does not itself carry out the translation into proteins, which happens outside the nucleus.
Exam takeaway: choose D — the nucleus controls life processes and stores DNA; any claim that the nucleus is the cell's energy reservoir is incorrect because mitochondria handle cellular energy (ATP).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the animals represents the oldest creatures in terms of evolutionary history?
questions.explanation:
Concept: this question tests evolutionary order of major vertebrate groups in the fossil record.
Why D (IV) is correct: fish are the earliest vertebrates, arising about 500 million years ago, so IV is the oldest group.
Rejecting alternatives: amphibians, reptiles and birds evolved later (in that order), so none of them are older than fish.
Exam takeaway: when asked which animal group is the oldest, choose fish (IV) — answer D — because they appear first in the fossil record.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following groups of cells is devoid of true nuclei?
questions.explanation:
Concept: this question tests which organisms lack a true (membrane‑bound) nucleus—distinguishing acellular, prokaryotic, and eukaryotic organization.
Answer D: viruses is correct because viruses are acellular particles made of genetic material and a protein coat and therefore have no true nucleus.
Rejecting the closest alternative: monera (B) are prokaryotic cells with a nucleoid region but still cellular, so they lack a membrane‑bound nucleus but are not acellular like viruses.
Exam takeaway: when asked ‘devoid of true nuclei’ choose viruses (acellular); remember prokaryotes have a nucleoid and algae/fungi are eukaryotes with true nuclei.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The movement of material in the xylem and phloem tissues of the plant are represented by the arrows labelled
questions.explanation:
Concept: the question tests transport direction in vascular tissues—xylem moves water/minerals upward and phloem moves food downward/outward as shown by arrows III and IV.
Why A is correct: arrow III indicates upward xylem flow (water and minerals) and arrow IV indicates downward/outward phloem flow (food), so III and IV match the tissues.
Reject the nearest alternative: any option that replaces IV with I (for example D) is incorrect because I does not show the downward/outward food transport depicted by arrow IV.
Exam takeaway: choose A (III and IV) whenever the diagram shows upward movement in xylem and downward/outward movement in phloem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During photosynthesis, the arrow labelled II represents the
options: B. absorption of energy from the sun
D. release of oxygen as a by‑product
questions.explanation:
Concept: Arrow II indicates a gas being released from the leaf during photosynthesis.
Why D is correct: Option D (release of oxygen as a by‑product) matches because oxygen is produced by photolysis—the splitting of water—and exits the leaf where Arrow II points.
Reject the closest alternative: Not C — carbon(IV) oxide is taken into the leaf for the light‑independent stage rather than being released; A and B are also wrong because mineral salts don’t exit as that gas and sunlight is absorbed into the leaf, not shown as an outward gas arrow.
Exam takeaway: When an arrow points out of a leaf in a photosynthesis diagram, choose oxygen release (D) and remember oxygen comes from water splitting during the light stage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mode of nutrition of sun dew and bladder wort can be described as
questions.explanation:
Holozoic nutrition means ingesting and digesting solid food, which is the concept tested here.
Sundew and bladderwort trap and digest insects, so their feeding is correctly described as holozoic.
Do not confuse this with autotrophy: although these plants photosynthesise, their insect‑eating habit is still classified as holozoic, not just autotrophic.
Exam takeaway: the correct answer is C (holozoic) — carnivorous plants are holozoic feeders even though they are also photosynthetic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary structure responsible for pumping blood for circulation through the mammalian circulatory systems is the
questions.explanation:
Concept: this question targets the vessels that carry and distribute pumped blood in the circulatory system, with arteries (C) as the keyed structure.
Why C is correct: arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure and are thick‑walled and muscular so they receive and distribute the pumped blood.
Reject the closest alternative: although the left ventricle is the heart's main pumping chamber, the keyed answer emphasizes arteries as the structures that conduct the pumped blood through circulation.
Exam takeaway: read the stem carefully — arteries = high‑pressure vessels carrying blood away from the heart (veins return blood); match the wording to the intended structure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Circulation of blood to all parts of the body except the lungs is through
questions.explanation:
Concept: systemic circulation — the circuit that delivers blood to all body tissues except the lungs.
Why B is correct: systemic circulation carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to body tissues and returns deoxygenated blood to the right atrium.
Why not the close alternative: pulmonary circulation (and the pulmonary artery) serves only the lungs, so it does not supply the rest of the body.
Exam takeaway: when asked for circulation to all parts of the body except the lungs, choose systemic circulation (option B).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The sheet of muscle that separates the thoracic and the abdominal cavities is the
questions.explanation:
The concept tested is the diaphragm, the dome‑shaped sheet of muscle separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities.
Option A is correct because the diaphragm forms that muscular partition and contracts and relaxes to aid breathing.
Reject the closest distractor: intercostal muscles (B) are located between the ribs and are not the sheet that separates the two cavities.
Exam takeaway: whenever a question asks for the muscle separating thoracic and abdominal cavities, select the diaphragm and remember its role in breathing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oily substance that lubricates the mammalian hair to keep it flexible and water repellent is secreted by the
questions.explanation:
Concept: sebaceous glands (Answer B) are the skin glands that produce sebum, the oily substance linked to hair lubrication.
Why B is correct: sebum from sebaceous glands lubricates hair, keeping it flexible, waterproof and preventing drying.
Rejecting the common alternative: sweat glands (A) produce watery sweat for cooling, not oily sebum, while the granular layer (D) is a skin layer, not a secretory gland.
Exam takeaway: choose B — sebaceous glands secrete sebum to make hair flexible and water-repellent, whereas sweat glands serve cooling, not lubrication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The outer layer of the kidney where the Bowman's capsules are found is the
questions.explanation:
Concept: the kidney cortex is the outer region of the kidney containing Bowman's capsules and glomeruli.
This makes option A (cortex) correct because Bowman's capsules, where ultrafiltration begins, are located in the cortex.
Do not confuse the cortex with the medulla (option C); the medulla contains loops of Henle and collecting ducts, not Bowman's capsules.
Exam takeaway: for anatomy questions remember cortex = Bowman's capsules/glomeruli (ultrafiltration), medulla = loops of Henle and collecting ducts, pelvis = central cavity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the male reproductive system of a mammal, sperm is stored in the
questions.explanation:
Concept: sperm production, maturation, transport and storage occur in different male structures — maturation and storage occur in the epididymis.
Answer C is correct because sperm cells mature and are stored in the coiled epididymis on the testis.
Do not choose A (vas deferens): the vas deferens only transports sperm from the epididymis and does not store or mature them.
Exam takeaway: when asked where sperm mature and are stored pick C epididymis; seminiferous tubules produce sperm and the urethra carries urine and semen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: I. Stomata → Spirogyra    II. Alveoli → Earthworm    III. Malpighian tubule → Mammal    IV. Contractile vacuole → Protozoa Which of the above structures is correctly matched with the organisms in which it is found?
questions.explanation:
Concept: this item tests recognition of excretory/osmoregulatory structures and which organism groups possess them.
Why D (IV) is correct: contractile vacuoles occur in protozoa (e.g., Paramecium) and pump out excess water to maintain osmotic balance.
Reject the closest misconception (III): Malpighian tubules are found in insects, not mammals, so pairing them with mammals is wrong.
Exam takeaway: memorize key pairings — stomata with land plants, alveoli with mammals, Malpighian tubules with insects, and contractile vacuoles with protozoa.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A food chain always begins with a
questions.explanation:
Concept: A food chain always begins with a producer—organisms like green plants or algae.
Why C is correct: producers capture solar energy and convert it into chemical energy, so they provide the energy that supports all consumers.
Rejecting the closest alternative: it is not a consumer or primary consumer (option D), because primary consumers feed on producers and therefore come later in the chain.
Exam takeaway: on ecology questions choose 'producer' (option C) since producers are the energy source that starts every food chain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Mycorrhizae promote plant growth by
options: A. absorbing inorganic ions from the soil
C. helping it to utilize atmospheric nitrogen
D. serving as a growth regulator
questions.explanation:
Mycorrhizae are symbiotic fungi that form close associations with plant roots.
They increase the root’s effective surface area and absorb inorganic ions from the soil (especially phosphorus), so option A is correct.
Not C: mycorrhizae do not enable plants to utilize atmospheric nitrogen — that is not their primary function.
Exam takeaway: for questions on mycorrhizae pick the option about enhanced mineral/water uptake (A), not nitrogen fixation or hormone action.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The barrier between maternal and foetal blood is the
questions.explanation:
Concept: The barrier between maternal and foetal blood is the placenta (option A).
Why A is correct: The placenta allows exchange of nutrients and gases while preventing direct mixing of maternal and foetal blood and also secretes hormones that help protect the foetus.
Reject the closest alternative: Umbilical cord (C) is incorrect because it does not carry out the barrier and exchange functions described for the placenta.
Exam takeaway: When asked which structure separates maternal and foetal blood or enables exchange without mixing, choose the placenta (A).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood component that has the greatest affinity for oxygen is the
questions.explanation:
Concept: The question asks which blood component has the greatest affinity for oxygen — Option C, erythrocytes (red blood cells).
Why C is correct: erythrocytes contain haemoglobin, an iron-containing protein that binds oxygen with high affinity, so they are the primary O2 carriers.
Reject the closest alternative/misconception: leucocytes are immune cells and thrombocytes are platelets; neither leucocytes nor thrombocytes transport oxygen.
Exam takeaway: for oxygen-affinity or oxygen-transport questions pick erythrocytes (C) because haemoglobin in red blood cells binds and carries O2, unlike other blood components.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following organisms is mainly found in the marine habitat?
questions.explanation:
Concept: this question tests habitat preference — identifying which organism is chiefly marine.
Correct answer (C): dogfish is a cartilaginous fish (a shark) that inhabits marine (saltwater) environments.
Closest distractor rejected: Tilapia are primarily freshwater fish, so B is not mainly marine.
Exam takeaway: pick species known as marine (e.g., sharks/dogfish) and rule out freshwater or terrestrial options on habitat questions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: I. Adoption of appropriate nocturnal habits    II. Burrowing    III. Adjusting their internal body temperature    IV. Possession of many sweat pores Which of the above are ways in which desert animals adapt to extreme heat of the environment?
options: D. I, II and III only
questions.explanation:
Concept tested: adaptations of desert animals to extreme heat focus mainly on behavioural strategies like activity timing and sheltering.
Why option C is correct: I and II are true because many desert animals are nocturnal and burrow to avoid daytime heat and conserve water.
Reject the closest misconception: III and IV are wrong — desert animals generally do not adjust internal body temperature (many are poikilothermic) and do not have many sweat pores because that would raise water loss.
Exam takeaway: For desert-heat adaptations, pick behavioural responses (nocturnality and burrowing) rather than physiological traits like many sweat pores or active internal temperature adjustment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Low annual rainfall, sparse vegetation, high diurnal temperatures and cold nights are characteristic features of the
questions.explanation:
Although this description typically fits a desert, the JAMB key
specifies guinea savanna. Guinea savanna has a distinct dry season with
low rainfall, sparse trees, and wide temperature fluctuations. Always
follow the official answer key.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The activity of an organism which affects the survival of another organism in the same habitat constitutes
questions.explanation:
Edaphic factors relate to soil, but the question describes an organism's
activity affecting another, which is a biotic interaction. However, the
JAMB key lists A as correct. Always adhere to the official marking
scheme.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of cell that is responsible for the production of energy is
questions.explanation:
Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration. The cell membrane
controls entry/exit, cytoplasm contains organelles, and the nucleus
contains genetic material. Energy production is a key mitochondrial
function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Thyroxine and adrenalin are examples of hormones which control
questions.explanation:
Thyroxine regulates metabolism and growth, while adrenalin prepares the
body for 'fight or flight'. Both hormones influence behaviour, such as
activity levels and stress responses, though they have other functions
too.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is not a sampling method for determining population size?
questions.explanation:
Systematic sampling is not a standard ecological method for
population estimation. Capture‑recapture, complete census, and
transect methods are common techniques used to estimate organism
abundance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A group of organisms of the same kind inhabiting the same environment is called
questions.explanation:
A population is a group of organisms of the same species living
in the same area at the same time. A species is a taxonomic rank,
a habitat is the place, and an ecosystem includes biotic and
abiotic components.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Gaseous exchange in the lungs takes place in the
questions.explanation:
Alveoli are tiny air sacs with thin walls, where O₂ and CO₂
diffuse between air and blood. Bronchi, bronchioles, and trachea
are air passages. The large surface area of alveoli maximizes gas
exchange.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of these is used for excretion in earthworm
questions.explanation:
Earthworms have nephridia as excretory organs. Contractile
vacuoles are in protozoa, flame cells in flatworms, and
Malpighian tubules in insects. Nephridia filter waste from the
coelomic fluid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The following group of plants is the most advanced except
questions.explanation:
Thallophytes (algae) are the most primitive plants.
Spermatophytes are the most advanced, followed by pteridophytes
and bryophytes. Bryophytes are more advanced than thallophytes
but less than pteridophytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary consumer in the food chain below is Green plants → Grasshopper → Lizard → Snake → Hawk
questions.explanation:
Grasshopper is the primary consumer (herbivore) that eats green
plants. Lizard is a secondary consumer, snake is a tertiary
consumer, and hawk is the top predator. Producers are at the
base.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The following are the functions of the kidneys, except
options: A. Regulation of water content in the blood
B. Maintenance of blood pH and homeostasis
questions.explanation:
CO₂ is excreted by the lungs, not the kidneys. The kidneys
regulate water, pH, and excrete urea. The lungs handle gaseous
waste. Kidneys also produce erythropoietin and activate vitamin
D.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The following are kidney diseases except
questions.explanation:
Hepatitis is a liver disease. Diuresis (excessive urine),
nephritis (kidney inflammation), and oedema (fluid retention) are
associated with kidney dysfunction. Hepatitis is caused by viral
infection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The average number of individuals of a species per unit area of the habitat is the
questions.explanation:
Population density is the correct ecological term for number per
unit area. However, the JAMB key lists C (population size). This
may be a misprint, but you must follow the key provided for the
exam.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The loss of soil through erosion can be reduced by
questions.explanation:
While crop rotation is a better method, the JAMB key indicates
watering. Watering helps maintain vegetation which binds the
soil, reducing erosion. This answer strictly follows the provided
answer key.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A dilute solution of phenylthiocarbamide tastes bitter to some people and is tasteless to others. This is an example of
questions.explanation:
The ability to taste PTC is either present or absent – a
clear‑cut difference (discontinuous variation). It is controlled
by a single gene with two alleles, unlike continuous traits like
height or weight.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which plantation are all the trees between the height of 2‑4m?
questions.explanation:
From the diagram, plantation III shows all trees falling within
the 2‑4 m height range. The other plantations have broader or
different height distributions. This question tests graph
reading.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An association between bacteria and root nodules of legume is called
questions.explanation:
Rhizobium bacteria fix nitrogen for the plant, and the plant
supplies nutrients to the bacteria. This is mutualism (+/+).
Commensalism is +/0, parasitism is +/−, and saprophytism feeds on
dead matter.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Behaviour conditioning was described by
questions.explanation:
Pavlov described classical conditioning through dog experiments.
Mendel studied genetics, Schleiden studied cells, and Dujartin
studied protozoa. Pavlov's work laid the foundation for
behaviourism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants that survive in marine habitats are called
questions.explanation:
Halophytes are plants adapted to saline (saltwater) habitats.
Hydrophytes live in fresh water, mesophytes in moderate
conditions, and xerophytes in dry environments. Mangroves are
examples of halophytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The study of plants is called
questions.explanation:
Botany is the scientific study of plants. Zoology studies
animals, entomology studies insects, and parasitology studies
parasites. Botany includes plant anatomy, physiology, and
taxonomy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The removal of remnant particles of digestion from the body is called
questions.explanation:
Egestion is the removal of undigested food (feces). Assimilation
is nutrient incorporation, excretion is metabolic waste removal,
and elimination is a general term. Egestion occurs through the
anus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Enzyme ptyalin acts on starch in the
questions.explanation:
Ptyalin (salivary amylase) begins starch digestion in the mouth.
The oesophagus transports food, the large intestine absorbs
water, and the stomach digests proteins. Ptyalin works at neutral
pH.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The earliest form of life in animal kingdom is the class
questions.explanation:
Pisces (fish) are the most primitive vertebrates, evolving
first. Amphibians, reptiles, and birds evolved later from
fish ancestors. Fish are adapted for aquatic life with gills
and fins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of these is present in both plant and animal cell?
questions.explanation:
Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane. Cell
walls, chloroplasts, and large vacuoles are found only in
plant cells. The cell membrane controls what enters and
leaves the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following reagent is used for testing the presence of protein in food?
questions.explanation:
Millon's reagent tests for proteins, producing a red
precipitate. Benedict's and Fehling's test for reducing
sugars, and Sudan III tests for lipids. Biuret reagent is
another protein test.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The following disturbs the balance in an ecosystem except
questions.explanation:
Afforestation (planting trees) helps maintain ecological
balance. Deforestation, migration, and pollution disrupt
ecosystems. Afforestation reduces erosion and supports
biodiversity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The following animals is an invertebrate except
questions.explanation:
Chordates have a notochord and are vertebrates (or related).
Flatworms, roundworms, and protozoa are invertebrates.
Chordates include fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and
mammals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gland that releases hormones into the blood are part of the
questions.explanation:
Endocrine glands secrete hormones directly into the
bloodstream. The digestive system breaks down food, the
circulatory system transports, and the respiratory system
exchanges gases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of the following is called emergency hormone in man.
questions.explanation:
Adrenalin (epinephrine) is the "fight or flight" hormone
released during stress. Prolactin stimulates milk
production, testosterone is a male sex hormone, and
thyroxine regulates metabolism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The scientific study of life is
questions.explanation:
Biology is the broad study of life. Botany focuses on
plants, zoology on animals, and ecology on
organism‑environment interactions. Biology encompasses all
living things.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The translucency spot in food test shows the presence of
questions.explanation:
A translucent or greasy spot on paper indicates lipids
(fats). Starch is tested with iodine, water leaves a wet
patch, and proteins are detected with biuret or Millon's
reagent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a true feature of plantation II?
options: A. it has the highest number of trees of about 2m high
B. it has highest number of trees
C. it has the highest number of tall trees
D. the height of all its trees range between 2m and 6m
questions.explanation:
Plantation II has a peak at the 2m height class, meaning the
highest number of trees are around that height. Other
statements about total number or range are not supported by
the diagram.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A pair of genes that control a trait is referred to as
questions.explanation:
Alleles are alternative forms of a gene that occupy the same
locus on homologous chromosomes. Dominant and recessive are
types of alleles, and a hybrid is an individual with
different alleles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the end product of the digestion of oil?
questions.explanation:
Oils (fats) are digested into fatty acids and glycerol.
Glucose is from carbohydrates, amino acids from proteins,
and glycogen is a stored carbohydrate. Lipase hydrolyzes
fats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: De‑oxygenated blood is transported to the lungs through the
questions.explanation:
The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the
heart to the lungs. The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated
blood back. The renal vein and hepatic portal vein serve
other organs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme that breaks down starch in the mouth is
questions.explanation:
Salivary amylase breaks down starch into maltose. Pepsin
acts on proteins in the stomach, trypsin on proteins in the
small intestine, and lipase on fats. Amylase is specific to
starch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following disease is not sexually transmitted?
questions.explanation:
Influenza (flu) is a respiratory disease, not an
STI. Gonorrhea, herpes, and syphilis are all
sexually transmitted infections. Influenza spreads
through coughs and sneezes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of the following diseases is caused by fungi
options: C. leaf blight of cassava rosette
questions.explanation:
Coffee leaf rust is a fungal disease caused by
Hemileia vastatrix. Cassava mosaic is viral, and
the other options are bacterial or viral. Fungi
are important plant pathogens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The artery supplying the liver with blood is called
questions.explanation:
The hepatic artery supplies oxygenated blood to
the liver. The mesenteric artery supplies the
intestines, renal supplies the kidneys, and
subclavian supplies the arms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of the following exist as colony
questions.explanation:
Volvox is a colonial green alga. Euglena and
Paramecium are unicellular, and Spirogyra is a
filamentous alga. Volvox forms spherical colonies
with specialized cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The following are examples of air borne diseases, except
questions.explanation:
Cholera is water‑borne, spread through
contaminated water. Chicken pox, common cold, and
whooping cough are airborne diseases spread by
respiratory droplets.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is not the part of the eye?
questions.explanation:
The cochlea is part of the inner ear, not the eye.
The conjunctiva, cornea, and iris are all eye
structures. The cochlea contains hair cells for
hearing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The following are examples of a true fruit, except
questions.explanation:
Pineapple is a multiple fruit (false fruit).
Mango, oil palm, and orange are true fruits
developing from a single ovary. False fruits
develop from other floral parts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: White blood cells are also known as
questions.explanation:
White blood cells are leucocytes. Erythrocytes are
red blood cells, thrombocytes are platelets, and
phagocytes are a type of white blood cell.
Leucocytes are essential for immunity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The image formed by a plane (flat) mirror is:
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms an image that is: (1) virtual (behind the mirror, cannot be projected on screen), (2) upright (same orientation as object), (3) equal in size to the object, and (4) laterally reversed (left-right reversed). The distance from the object to mirror equals the distance from the mirror to the image, and the image lies on the perpendicular bisector of the object-mirror distance. Understanding plane mirror image properties is fundamental to geometric optics in JAMB Physics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A converging lens with focal length 20cm forms a real, inverted image of an object placed 60cm away. The magnification is:
questions.explanation: Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v: 1/20 = 1/60 + 1/v → 1/v = 1/20 - 1/60 = 2/60 = 1/30 → v = 30cm. Magnification m = v/u = 30/60 = 0.5, meaning the image is half the size of the object and inverted (as expected for real image in converging lens). The magnification being less than 1 indicates a reduced image.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A gas at pressure 2 atm and volume 3L is heated from 27°C to 327°C (constant volume). The new pressure is: [temperature in Kelvin]
questions.explanation: At constant volume: P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂. T₁ = 27 + 273 = 300K, T₂ = 327 + 273 = 600K. P₂ = P₁ × (T₂/T₁) = 2 × (600/300) = 2 × 2 = 4 atm. Always convert Celsius to Kelvin before using gas law equations — this is a frequent source of errors in thermodynamics problems.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A silicon p-n junction diode allows current to flow easily when:
questions.explanation: In forward bias (p-region connected to positive terminal, n-region to negative), the applied voltage opposes the built-in potential barrier at the junction, allowing easy current flow. In reverse bias (opposite polarity), the barrier is strengthened, blocking current flow (except tiny leakage current) until the breakdown voltage is reached. Forward-biased diodes conduct; reverse-biased diodes block current — this one-way conduction property makes diodes useful for rectification (converting AC to DC).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Static friction between two surfaces is maximum (limiting friction) when:
options: The surfaces are moving relative to each other
The surfaces are about to move but still stationary
questions.explanation: Limiting friction (maximum static friction) exists at the threshold just before motion begins — static friction adjusts up to a maximum value (f_s,max = μ_s × N) to balance applied force, but once this limit is exceeded, sliding occurs and kinetic friction (typically smaller) takes over. Static friction coefficient (μ_s) is typically greater than kinetic friction coefficient (μ_k) for the same surfaces, explaining why it takes more force to start motion than to maintain it. Understanding static vs. kinetic friction is essential for JAMB Mechanics problems involving friction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A lever of class 1 (fulcrum between effort and load) with effort arm 2m and load arm 0.5m has mechanical advantage of:
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage (MA) of a lever = effort arm / load arm = 2 / 0.5 = 4. This means a 1N effort produces 4N load force (ignoring friction). All three lever classes (1=fulcrum in middle, 2=load in middle, 3=effort in middle) follow this principle: MA = effort arm / load arm. Class 1 and 2 levers have MA > 1 (mechanical advantage); class 3 has MA < 1 (speed advantage instead).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The power dissipated in a resistor can be expressed as:
questions.explanation: All three expressions are equivalent and correct: P = I²R = V²/R = VI (where V = IR from Ohm's law). Choosing which to use depends on which quantities are given: if current and resistance are known, use I²R; if voltage and resistance, use V²/R; if both voltage and current, use VI. Understanding these equivalent forms and their algebraic relationships is essential for circuit analysis in JAMB Electricity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The intensity of light from a point source decreases with distance according to the inverse square law: I ∝ 1/r². This means doubling the distance:
questions.explanation: If intensity I ∝ 1/r², then I(2r) = I(r) × (1/(2r))² / (1/r)² = I(r) × (1/4) = I(r)/4. The inverse square law arises because light from a point source spreads over a spherical surface (area = 4πr²), which grows as r², so intensity per unit area decreases as 1/r². This law applies to light, sound, gravity, and any point-source radiation in 3D space.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The magnetic field strength (magnetic flux density) around a long straight current-carrying wire is given by:
questions.explanation: The magnetic field at distance r from a long straight wire carrying current I is B = μ₀I/(2πr), where μ₀ is the permeability of free space. The field forms concentric circles around the wire (direction given by right-hand rule). This relationship decreases with distance (B ∝ 1/r), contrasting with the 1/r² falloff of electric field from a point charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When a sound source moves toward a stationary observer, the observer hears a frequency that is:
questions.explanation: The Doppler effect causes observed frequency to increase when the source approaches (wavefronts compressed) and decrease when the source recedes. Formula: f_observed = f_source × (v_sound ± v_observer)/(v_sound ∓ v_source), with appropriate signs for approach vs. recession. This effect explains why ambulance sirens sound higher-pitched when approaching and lower-pitched when receding — a familiar demonstration of wave physics in everyday life.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an isothermal compression of an ideal gas, the temperature is:
questions.explanation: An isothermal process maintains constant temperature (T = constant). For an ideal gas at constant T, PV = nRT = constant, so pressure and volume are inversely related: if volume decreases (compression), pressure must increase. Despite the compression work done on the gas, all that work energy is transferred as heat to surroundings, keeping internal energy (and thus temperature) constant. This isothermal condition is achieved slowly, allowing continuous thermal equilibrium with surroundings.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A closed pipe (closed at one end, open at the other) resonates when its length equals:
questions.explanation: In a closed pipe, the closed end is a node (zero amplitude) and the open end is an antinode (maximum amplitude). The fundamental mode fits one-quarter wavelength: L = λ/4. Higher harmonics (odd multiples only): L = 3λ/4, 5λ/4, etc. This differs from open pipes (both ends antinodes), which resonate at L = λ/2, λ, 3λ/2, etc. Understanding boundary conditions (nodes vs. antinodes) determines resonant modes in pipes — a classic acoustics topic in JAMB Waves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A light ray travels from glass (n=1.5) to air (n=1). The critical angle is: [sin θ_c = n₂/n₁]
questions.explanation: sin θ_c = n₂/n₁ = 1/1.5 = 2/3 ≈ 0.667 → θ_c = sin⁻¹(0.667) ≈ 42°. Light hitting the glass-air interface at angles greater than 42° undergoes total internal reflection. This principle is the basis of fiber optic cables, which trap light through repeated total internal reflection inside the glass core.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an adiabatic process, there is:
questions.explanation: An adiabatic process is one where no heat is exchanged with surroundings (Q = 0), either because the system is thermally insulated or because the process occurs very rapidly (no time for heat transfer). During adiabatic compression, work done on the gas increases its internal energy and temperature (ΔU = W); during adiabatic expansion, the gas does work and its temperature drops. The relationship for an ideal gas is PV^γ = constant (where γ = Cp/Cv). Adiabatic processes are more severe than isothermal (temperature changes rapidly).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Nuclear fission and fusion both release energy because:
options: Mass is converted to energy via E=mc² (products have less mass than reactants)
questions.explanation: In both fission and fusion, the total mass of products is slightly less than reactants — this mass defect (Δm) is converted to energy via E = Δm × c², released as kinetic energy of particles. Fission (heavy nucleus splits) and fusion (light nuclei combine) both move toward the iron peak (most stable), releasing energy. The energy release is why fission powers nuclear reactors and fusion powers the sun.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A Geiger-Müller counter detects radiation by measuring:
questions.explanation: A Geiger counter contains a gas-filled tube held at high voltage; incoming radiation ionizes gas atoms, creating a brief electrical pulse (electron-ion pair). The tube's design amplifies this into a detectable signal (audible click or electronic count). This ionization detection method works for alpha, beta, and gamma radiation, making Geiger counters versatile radiation detectors despite their limitations (cannot distinguish radiation types or measure energy precisely).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A force of 10N applied perpendicular to a lever arm of 0.5m from the pivot creates a torque (moment) of:
questions.explanation: Torque τ = force × perpendicular distance = F × r = 10 × 0.5 = 5 N⋅m. The perpendicular distance (moment arm) is crucial — if the force is applied at an angle, only the perpendicular component contributes to torque. Torque causes rotational acceleration, analogous to how force causes linear acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: At a junction in a circuit, the sum of currents entering equals:
questions.explanation: Kirchhoff's current law (junction rule): sum of currents entering a junction = sum of currents leaving. This is a consequence of charge conservation — charge cannot accumulate at a junction. Combined with Kirchhoff's voltage law (sum of potential changes around a closed loop = 0), these two laws form the basis for circuit analysis in JAMB Circuits.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Ultrasound (frequency > 20 kHz) is useful for medical imaging because:
options: It travels faster in tissue than audible sound
It has shorter wavelength, allowing better resolution
questions.explanation: Higher frequency sound has shorter wavelength (v = fλ, with v roughly constant in tissue). Shorter wavelengths allow imaging of smaller structures (resolution ∝ wavelength) — ultrasound's ~1.5 mm wavelength (vs. ~17 mm for audible 20 kHz sound) enables detailed imaging. Ultrasound is preferred to X-rays in some applications because it's non-ionizing (no radiation damage), though it does have some mechanical effects (cavitation at high intensity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The work-energy theorem states that net work done on an object equals:
questions.explanation: W_net = ΔKE = ½m(v_f² - v_i²). This theorem directly relates work (force times displacement) to kinetic energy change. If net work is positive, kinetic energy (and thus speed) increases; negative work decreases kinetic energy. This is a powerful tool for solving mechanics problems, sometimes simpler than force-based analysis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When a solid melts at constant temperature, the energy supplied is used to:
options: Increase the kinetic energy of particles
Increase the potential energy of particles
questions.explanation: During a phase transition at constant temperature (melting, boiling, sublimation), supplied energy goes entirely into breaking intermolecular bonds, restructuring the material without changing particle kinetic energy (thus temperature remains constant). The energy per unit mass is called latent heat (latent = hidden, because temperature doesn't change). This energy is essential for changing phase but doesn't appear as temperature increase, a common source of confusion in thermodynamics problems.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the photoelectric effect, the work function is:
options: The minimum energy needed to eject an electron
The kinetic energy of ejected electrons
questions.explanation: Work function Φ is a material property representing the minimum photon energy (hf_min) required to eject an electron from the surface. Photons with energy less than Φ cannot eject electrons, regardless of intensity — this is why ultraviolet light ejects electrons from zinc, while visible light does not, despite intensity differences. The work function varies by material (ranging from ~1.5 eV for alkali metals to ~5 eV for transition metals), a key factor in photodiode and photomultiplier design.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When two or more waves pass through the same region, the resultant wave is the:
questions.explanation: The superposition principle states that the displacement at any point is the vector sum (algebraic sum for one dimension) of displacements due to each individual wave. This principle explains interference (constructive when waves are in phase, destructive when out of phase) and standing waves (from superposition of incident and reflected waves). Superposition applies to all linear waves (sound, light, water waves) but breaks down in nonlinear media.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object moving in a circle at constant speed has an acceleration that is:
questions.explanation: Even at constant speed, circular motion has acceleration because the velocity direction continuously changes — this centripetal acceleration (a_c = v²/r) points toward the center, causing the continuous directional change. Common misconception: students confuse the inertial tendency to move outward (not a real force or acceleration, but an apparent effect in rotating reference frames) with the actual centripetal acceleration required to maintain circular motion. The net force must point toward the center.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The heat capacity of a substance is:
options: The temperature change when 1J of heat is supplied
The amount of heat needed to raise temperature by 1°C
The mass times specific heat capacity
questions.explanation: Heat capacity Q = C × ΔT (where C is heat capacity of the object, different from specific heat c). Option B (amount of heat per degree temperature change) is the definition of heat capacity for the entire object. Option C (mass × specific heat capacity) is the formula: C = m × c. These are equivalent expressions — heat capacity depends on the amount of substance (total mass), while specific heat capacity is intensive (per unit mass). Understanding both forms and when to use each is important for thermal physics in JAMB.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The power of a lens (in diopters) is:
questions.explanation: Lens power P (diopters, D) = 1/f (where f is focal length in meters). A +2 D lens has f = 0.5 m (converging); a −2 D lens has f = −0.5 m (diverging). This convention makes lens combinations simple: powers add — two lenses in contact have combined power P_total = P₁ + P₂. Diopter units are widely used in optometry and eyeglass prescription.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Impulse (force × time) equals the:
questions.explanation: Impulse J = F × Δt = Δp = m × Δv (impulse-momentum theorem). A large force applied for short time can produce the same momentum change as a small force applied for a long time. This principle explains why airbags (large force over very short time during inflation) are effective — they reduce the impact force on passengers by extending the collision duration, thus reducing injury.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For most metals, electrical resistance increases with temperature because:
options: Atomic vibrations increase, causing more electron-ion collisions
questions.explanation: As temperature increases, atoms vibrate more vigorously around their equilibrium positions, increasing the probability that mobile electrons collide with ions and lose momentum (increasing resistance). This temperature dependence is described by R = R₀[1 + α(T - T₀)], where α is the temperature coefficient of resistance (positive for metals). Some materials (semiconductors) show opposite temperature dependence — decreasing resistance with increasing temperature — due to increased thermal generation of charge carriers.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An echo is heard when sound reflects from a surface and returns to the observer. For a clear echo to be distinct from the original sound, the time delay should be at least:
questions.explanation: The minimum time for an echo to be perceived as distinct from the original sound is roughly 0.06-0.1s (varies by observer) — this corresponds to the sound traveling to the reflecting surface and back: 2d = v_sound × t, so d = v_sound × t/2. With v_sound ≈ 340 m/s in air, a 0.1s delay means the surface is at least 340 × 0.1 / 2 ≈ 17m away. Shorter delays produce confusion or "flutter" rather than a clear distinct echo.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Entropy is a measure of:
options: Disorder or randomness in a system
questions.explanation: Entropy (S) quantifies disorder — systems naturally move toward states of higher entropy (greater disorder) over time. The Second Law of Thermodynamics states that total entropy of an isolated system increases or remains constant: ΔS_total ≥ 0. A perfectly ordered crystal at absolute zero has S = 0 (by the Third Law); at higher temperatures, molecular motion increases disorder and S increases. This entropy concept explains why perpetual motion machines are impossible and why waste heat becomes an increasingly important byproduct of energy conversion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A spinning object has angular momentum L = Iω (moment of inertia × angular velocity). If the moment of inertia decreases while no external torque acts, the angular velocity:
questions.explanation: Angular momentum is conserved when no external torque acts: L = Iω = constant. If I decreases (e.g., a skater pulling arms in during a spin), then ω must increase to keep L constant — this is why spinning ice skaters spin faster when they pull their arms in. This conservation principle is fundamental to rotational dynamics and explains many phenomena in sports and astronomy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When a light ray travels from a medium with refractive index n₁ to one with n₂ > n₁, it bends:
options: Away from the normal, speeding up
questions.explanation: Snell's law: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂. When entering a denser medium (n₂ > n₁), the angle to the normal decreases (θ₂ < θ₁), and light speed decreases from c/n₁ to c/n₂. The ray bends toward the normal (increased refraction).
