questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A common characteristic of copper and silver in their usage as coinage metals is that they
questions.explanation: The property that actually makes a metal suitable for coinage is corrosion resistance — coins need to survive years of handling without rusting or tarnishing away. Copper and silver are both relatively unreactive ('noble') metals low on the reactivity series, which is exactly why they (along with gold) have been used for coinage throughout history.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Haematite is an ore of
questions.explanation: Haematite is iron (III) oxide, Fe2O3 — one of the most important iron ores, and a straightforward recall fact worth just knowing directly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The least easily oxidized of the metals below is
questions.explanation: Place these on the reactivity series: Na and Ca are group 1 and 2 metals, both highly reactive and easily oxidized. Al is reactive too, though less so. Zinc sits lower still, making it the least easily oxidized (least reactive) of the four listed here.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The repeating unit in natural rubber is
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is a polymer built from repeating isoprene units (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) — this monomer, linked together thousands of times, is exactly what gives rubber its elastic, coiled polymer structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Unsaturated organic compounds are identified by decolourization of
options: silver bromide and potassium tetraoxomanganate (VII) solution
bromine water and acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate (VII) solution
silver bromide solution and bromine water
bromine water and alkaline potassium tetraoxomanganate (VII) solution
questions.explanation: Two standard tests confirm unsaturation (a C=C or C≡C bond): bromine water decolourises via an addition reaction across the double/triple bond, and acidified (not alkaline) potassium tetraoxomanganate (VII) also decolourises by oxidizing across the same bond. The 'acidified' condition matters specifically — that's the classic test as usually taught.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The conditions necessary for the extraction of a water molecule from two molecules of ethanol are
options: less acid and a lower temperature
excess acid and a lower temperature
excess acid and a higher temperature
less acid and a higher temperature
questions.explanation: Removing water between two separate ethanol molecules is intermolecular dehydration, which forms an ether (diethyl ether). This is the low-temperature pathway (around 140°C), favoured when acid is relatively less concentrated so alcohol is effectively in excess. The alternative — one ethanol molecule losing water from within itself to form an alkene — needs excess concentrated acid and higher temperature (around 170°C). Mixing up these two conditions is the classic trap in this topic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The chlorinated alkane often used industrially to remove grease is
questions.explanation: Tetrachloromethane (carbon tetrachloride, CCl4) was historically the standard industrial degreasing solvent, valued for dissolving oils and greases effectively (though it's now heavily restricted due to toxicity — this is the classic exam fact, describing its historical industrial role).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of carbide with water gives
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide (CaC2) reacting with water is the classic industrial route to acetylene: CaC2 + 2H2O → C2H2 + Ca(OH)2. This is also literally how old carbide miners' lamps generated their fuel gas on demand.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: CH3-CH2-C(=O)-O-CH2-CH3. The compound above is an
questions.explanation: The C(=O)-O- linkage — a carbonyl carbon directly bonded to a single-bonded oxygen that connects to another carbon chain — is the defining ester functional group. An ether has no carbonyl at all (just C-O-C), an alkanal's carbonyl is at the end of the chain with an H attached, and an alkanol has an -OH group, none of which matches this structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Alkanones are generally obtained by the oxidation of
questions.explanation: Where oxidation stops depends on how many hydrogens are on the carbon bearing the -OH group. A secondary alcohol has exactly one hydrogen there, and oxidizing it removes that hydrogen to form a ketone (alkanone) — with no further hydrogen available, oxidation stops there. Primary alcohols have two such hydrogens and oxidize further, through an aldehyde and on to a carboxylic acid. Tertiary alcohols have no hydrogen on that carbon at all and can't be oxidized this way under normal conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Sucrose is made up of
questions.explanation: Sucrose (table sugar) is a disaccharide of one glucose unit and one fructose unit joined together. Keeping the common disaccharides straight: maltose is glucose+glucose, lactose is glucose+galactose, and sucrose is glucose+fructose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: 25cm3 of a gas X contains Z molecules at 15oC and 75 mm Hg. How many molecules will 25cm3 of another gas Y contain at the same temperature and pressure?
questions.explanation: This is Avogadro's law in its purest form: equal volumes of any gas, at the same temperature and pressure, contain equal numbers of molecules — regardless of what the gas actually is. Same volume, same T, same P, means same molecule count. Y's identity is irrelevant here.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What mass of water is produced when 8.0g of hydrogen reacts with excess oxygen?
questions.explanation: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O — the mole ratio of H2 to H2O is 1:1. Moles of H2 = 8.0/2 = 4 mol, so 4 mol of H2O forms. Mass of water = 4 × 18 = 72.0g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Four elements W, X, Y and Z have atomic numbers 2, 6, 16 and 20 respectively. Which of these elements is a metal?
questions.explanation: Place each atomic number on the periodic table: W (2) is helium, a noble gas. X (6) is carbon, a non-metal. Y (16) is sulphur, a non-metal. Z (20) is calcium, a genuine metal — a reactive group 2 element. Only Z fits.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An element X with relative atomic mass 16.2 contains two isotopes, 16-X with relative abundance of 90% and m-X with relative abundance of 10%. The value of m is
questions.explanation: The relative atomic mass is a weighted average: 16.2 = (0.90 × 16) + (0.10 × m). That gives 16.2 = 14.4 + 0.1m, so 0.1m = 1.8, and m = 18.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cancerous growth are cured by exposure to
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are the standard radiation used in cancer radiotherapy (cobalt-60 is a classic gamma source) — they penetrate deeply enough to reach internal tumours while damaging the rapidly-dividing cancer cells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the average kinetic energy of the molecules of a gas?
options: it increases with increase in pressure
it increases with increase in temperature
it increases with increase in volume
questions.explanation: Kinetic theory ties average kinetic energy directly to temperature and only temperature — it's essentially the definition of what temperature measures at the molecular level. Pressure and volume can change independently of kinetic energy (think of Boyle's law, done at constant temperature).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Millikan's contribution to the development of atomic theory is the determination of
questions.explanation: Millikan's famous oil-drop experiment measured the precise charge carried by a single electron. Keep the scientists straight: Thomson discovered the electron and measured its charge-to-mass ratio, Millikan pinned down its actual charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A particle that contains 9 protons, 10 neutrons and 10 electrons is
questions.explanation: 9 protons identifies the element as fluorine. A neutral fluorine atom would have 9 electrons to match its 9 protons — but this particle has 10 electrons, one more than protons, giving it an overall negative charge. That extra electron makes it F-, a negative ion, and fluorine is a non-metal that commonly forms anions this way.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An oxide XO2 has a vapour density of 32. What is the atomic mass of X?
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 2 × vapour density = 2 × 32 = 64. XO2's molar mass is X + 2(16) = X + 32. Setting that equal to 64: X = 64 - 32 = 32.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The chemical used for coagulation in water purification is
questions.explanation: Aluminium sulphate (alum) is the classic coagulant used in water treatment — the aluminium ions neutralize the charge on suspended particles, letting them clump together and settle out. None of the other metal sulphates listed do this job in standard water treatment.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Environmental pollution is worsened by the release from automobile exhausts of
questions.explanation: Heavy metals (historically lead, from leaded petrol additives) released in vehicle exhaust are the pollutant with the most serious, lasting environmental and health impact among the options — they don't break down and accumulate in the environment. Water vapour and steam are essentially harmless combustion byproducts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phosphorus is stored under water to prevent it from
questions.explanation: White phosphorus is pyrophoric — it spontaneously ignites in contact with air at room temperature. Storing it under water cuts off its access to oxygen, which is the whole reason for the precaution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Pure solvents are obtained by
questions.explanation: Distillation is the standard method to recover a pure solvent from a solution — evaporation drives off the solvent and loses it, while distillation vaporizes and then condenses it back into a pure, collected liquid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Deliquescent substances are used for
questions.explanation: Deliquescent substances (like anhydrous calcium chloride) absorb moisture from the air so avidly they eventually dissolve into a solution of their own absorbed water — which is exactly what makes them useful as drying agents, pulling moisture out of a gas or an enclosed space.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: What is the decrease in volume of air when pyrogallol is shaken with 30.00cm3 of air?
questions.explanation: Alkaline pyrogallol is a classic reagent that absorbs oxygen specifically out of a sample of air, leaving the rest (mostly nitrogen) behind. Oxygen makes up close to a fifth of air by volume, so the volume decrease should be roughly a fifth of 30cm3 — about 6cm3, matching 6.30cm3 here. This is worth remembering as a real lab technique for measuring the oxygen percentage in air, not just a number to memorize.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pollution from petroleum spillage in rivers and lakes can best be dispersed by
options: passing of ships through the area
questions.explanation: Detergents act as surfactants, breaking an oil slick into fine droplets that disperse through the water rather than sitting on top — this is the standard method used on real oil spills, not just a textbook answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 3Cu(s) + 8HNO3(aq) → 3Cu(NO3)2(aq) + 4H2O(l) + 2NO(g). In the equation above, copper is
questions.explanation: Copper goes from 0 (elemental metal) to +2 (in Cu(NO3)2) — it's losing electrons, which means it's being oxidized. A substance that gets oxidized itself is, by definition, the reducing agent — it reduces something else (here, nitrogen in HNO3 goes from +5 to +2 in NO) by donating those electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: NH3(g) + HCl(g) → NH4Cl(s). The entropy change in the system above is
questions.explanation: Two gas molecules combine into one solid — that's a dramatic decrease in disorder. Gas particles move freely and independently; a solid locks them into a fixed, ordered lattice. Fewer options for how the particles can be arranged means entropy has decreased, so ΔS is negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What current in amperes will deposit 2.7g of aluminum in 2 hours? [Al = 27, F = 96500 C mol-1]
questions.explanation: Moles of Al = 2.7/27 = 0.1 mol. Since Al3+ + 3e- → Al, depositing 1 mol of Al takes 3 mol of electrons, so 0.1 mol Al takes 0.3 mol electrons. Charge needed = 0.3 × 96500 = 28,950 C. Convert 2 hours to seconds: 2 × 3600 = 7200s. Current = charge/time = 28,950/7200 ≈ 4A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g). The yield of the reaction above is increased by
options: increasing the pressure of the system
increasing the temperature of the system
increasing the surface area of the vessel
the addition of a catalyst to the system
questions.explanation: Worth being precise here: pressure and temperature affect equilibrium differently. This reaction has 3 moles of gas on the left and 2 on the right, so increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium toward the side with fewer gas molecules (the product side), increasing the yield of SO3. That's a genuine shift in position — it does not change the equilibrium constant itself, which depends only on temperature. Since this reaction is exothermic forward, increasing temperature would actually shift equilibrium backward, reducing yield — so that's the wrong direction. A catalyst speeds up how fast equilibrium is reached but never changes the yield you end up with. 'Surface area of the vessel' isn't a real equilibrium variable at all.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: As the concentration of an electrolyte reduces, the conductivity
questions.explanation: Fewer dissolved ions per unit volume means fewer charge carriers available to conduct current — so at this level, less concentrated means less conductive, in a straightforward direct relationship.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: C(s) + 2S(g) → CS2, ΔH = 89 kJ mol-1. The chemical equation above implies that
options: each of carbon and sulphur has 89 kJ of energy
both carbon and sulphur contribute 89kJ of energy
questions.explanation: A positive ΔH means the reaction has to take in energy to proceed — that's the definition of endothermic. Carbon disulphide genuinely does have a positive standard enthalpy of formation in real data (around +89 kJ/mol), which matches what's given here.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following best explains the increase in the rate of a chemical reaction as the temperature rises?
options: A lower proportion of the molecules has the necessary minimum energy to react
The bonds in the reacting molecules are more readily broken
The collision frequency of the molecules increases
The molecular collisions become more violent
questions.explanation: As temperature rises, molecules move faster on average, which means they collide with each other more often — a genuine increase in collision frequency. (A fuller picture also includes that more of those collisions carry enough energy to actually react, but among these specific options, increased collision frequency is the correctly-stated mechanism.)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: P(g) + Q(g) ⇌ 3R(s) + S(g). Which of the following will increase the yield of R?
questions.explanation: R is a solid product, so it doesn't count toward the gas-phase equilibrium shift directly — but S is a gaseous product, and removing it pulls the equilibrium forward (Le Chatelier: the system reacts to replace what's been taken away), which means more P and Q convert into R and S. A larger vessel would lower the pressure, and since there are 2 mol of gas on the reactant side vs. 1 mol on the product side, lowering pressure actually favours the reactant side — the opposite of what's wanted. A catalyst never changes the yield, only the speed of reaching it. Increasing temperature's effect can't be determined without knowing the reaction's enthalpy, which isn't given.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethanoic acid is
questions.explanation: Basicity counts how many ionizable (replaceable) hydrogens an acid has. CH3COOH has only one such hydrogen — the one on the -COOH group, not the three on the methyl group — making it monobasic, just like HCl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A metal M displaces zinc from zinc chloride solution. This shows that
options: M is more electronegative than zinc
Zinc is above hydrogen in the series
Electron flow from zinc to M
M is more electropositive that zinc
questions.explanation: A metal that displaces another from its salt solution is the more reactive one — higher up the reactivity series, more willing to give up electrons. That reactivity is described as being more electropositive, not more electronegative (that term belongs to non-metals attracting electrons).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In which of the following reactions does reduction take place? A) 2O2- → O2 + 4e-; B) Fe2+ - e- → Fe3+; C) 2H+ + 2e- → H2; D) Cr - 2e- → Cr2+
questions.explanation: Reduction, remembered simply, is gain of electrons. Check each one: O2- losing electrons to become O2 is oxidation. Fe2+ losing an electron to become Fe3+ is oxidation. Cr losing electrons to become Cr2+ is oxidation. Only H+ gaining electrons to form H2 fits the definition of reduction — the H+ ions are gaining the electrons shown on the left side of the equation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When ΔH is negative, a reaction is said to be
questions.explanation: A negative ΔH means the products end up with less energy than the reactants started with — that missing energy has been released to the surroundings, which is the definition of exothermic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the hybridization of the carbon atom in ethyne?
questions.explanation: Ethyne (C2H2) has a carbon-carbon triple bond, and a triple bond always means sp hybridization: one sigma bond needs one hybrid orbital, and the two unhybridized p orbitals form the remaining two pi bonds of the triple bond. Count the bond type, not the molecule name: single bonds only → sp3, one double bond → sp2, a triple bond → sp.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Protein in acid solution undergo
questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds — acid (with water) breaks those bonds apart, splitting the protein back down into its amino acid building blocks. That water-driven breakdown is hydrolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Fermentation is the
options: breaking down of carbohydrate to glucose
breaking down of sugar to carbohydrate
conversion of sugar to alcohol in the presence of yeast
conversion of alcohol to sugar in the presence of yeast
questions.explanation: Fermentation, in the sense the JAMB syllabus means it, is yeast's zymase enzyme converting sugar (glucose) into ethanol and CO2 — the process behind brewing and baking.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Catalytic hydrogenation of benzene produces
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen across benzene's ring, fully saturating it — the 6-carbon aromatic ring becomes the 6-carbon fully saturated ring, cyclohexane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A characteristic reaction of the compounds with the general formula CnH2n is
questions.explanation: CnH2n is the alkene formula — unsaturated compounds with a reactive C=C double bond. Among these four options, polymerization is the one genuinely characteristic of alkenes: the double bond opens up and links many monomer units together (like ethene forming polyethene). Substitution is more characteristic of alkanes; esterification and decarboxylation are reactions of carboxylic acids, unrelated to the C=C bond that defines this formula.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When chlorine is passed into water and the resulting solution exposed to sunlight, the products formed are
questions.explanation: Chlorine dissolving in water first forms a mixture of HCl and HOCl (chloric(I)/hypochlorous acid). Sunlight then decomposes the unstable HOCl further, releasing oxygen and leaving HCl behind. This is exactly why chlorine water and bleach solutions are stored in dark containers — light breaks them down.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The pair of organic compounds that are isomers is
questions.explanation: Isomers share the exact same molecular formula but differ in structure. Only but-1-ene and but-2-ene share a formula — both are C4H8, just with the double bond in a different position. The other pairs all have genuinely different molecular formulas, so they can't be isomers, no matter how similar they look.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: C12H22O11(s) + H2SO4(aq) → 12C(s) + 11H2O(l) + H2SO4(aq). In the reaction above, tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid functions as
questions.explanation: This is the classic sugar-charring demonstration: concentrated sulphuric acid pulls the water (hydrogen and oxygen, in the exact ratio of water) directly out of sugar's structure, leaving behind a black mass of pure carbon. The acid itself appears unchanged on both sides of the equation, which is the signature of a dehydrating agent rather than a reactant being consumed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: During the vulcanization of rubber sulphur is added to
questions.explanation: Sulphur forms crosslinking bridges between neighbouring rubber polymer chains, tying separate chains together into a stronger, more elastic network — that crosslinking is exactly what vulcanization means.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When sodium reacts with water, the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2. Sodium hydroxide is a strong base, so the resulting solution is strongly alkaline — this is the whole reason sodium's reaction with water is a well-known, vigorous demonstration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The general formula for the alkanals is
questions.explanation: Alkanals (aldehydes) are defined by the -CHO group sitting at the end of a carbon chain — the carbonyl carbon still carries a hydrogen, which is exactly what distinguishes an aldehyde from a ketone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following metals burns with a brick red flame?
questions.explanation: Calcium's flame test signature is brick-red. Keep the common ones distinct: sodium is golden-yellow, potassium is lilac, calcium is brick-red.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The gas that can best be collected by downward displacement of air is
questions.explanation: 'Downward displacement of air' collects gases that are LESS dense than air — the jar is inverted (mouth down) and the light gas rises to fill it, pushing air out the bottom. Ammonia (molar mass 17) is the only gas here lighter than air (average molar mass ~29). Chlorine, SO2, and CO2 are all denser than air and would need the opposite method — upward displacement, jar mouth up.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A trihydric alkanol is
questions.explanation: 'Trihydric' means three -OH groups. Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) has exactly three, one per carbon. Ethanol has one (monohydric), glycol has two (dihydric), and phenol is a different class of compound entirely (an aromatic -OH, not a typical alkanol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The main impurity in iron ore during the extraction of iron is
questions.explanation: Silica (silicon(IV) oxide, sand) is the main gangue impurity found alongside iron ore. It's not itself reduced in the blast furnace — instead, limestone reacts with it to form calcium silicate (slag), which is removed separately. Calcium trioxosilicate is the SLAG formed to remove the impurity, not the impurity itself.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The formula CH2O for ethanoic acid is regarded as its
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid's actual molecular formula is C2H4O2 (CH3COOH) — CH2O is just its simplest whole-number atom ratio, which is exactly what 'empirical formula' means. The molecular formula would show the real atom count (C2H4O2); a structural formula would show how those atoms connect (CH3-COOH); a general formula describes a whole homologous series (like CnH2nO2 for carboxylic acids), not one specific compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following gases contains the least number of atoms at s.t.p?
questions.explanation: Convert each to total atoms: 7 mol Ar (monatomic) = 7 mol atoms. 4 mol Cl2 (diatomic) = 8 mol atoms. 3 mol O3 (triatomic) = 9 mol atoms. 1 mol C4H10 (14 atoms per molecule) = 14 mol atoms. 7 mol atoms from argon is the smallest of the four.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The chromatographic separation of ink is based on the ability of the components to
options: dissolve in each other in the column
move at different speeds in the column
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates a mixture because its components have different affinities for the stationary phase versus the mobile phase, so they travel at different speeds through the medium — components that cling less to the paper/column move faster and separate out from those that cling more.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A compound contains 31.91% potassium, 28.93% chlorine and the rest oxygen. What is the chemical formula of the compound?
questions.explanation: Oxygen % = 100 − 31.91 − 28.93 = 39.16%. Divide each by molar mass: K = 31.91/39 = 0.818; Cl = 28.93/35.5 = 0.815; O = 39.16/16 = 2.448. Dividing through by the smallest (0.815) gives a ratio of about 1 : 1 : 3, so the formula is KClO3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A little quantity of trichloromethane (b.pt. 60°C) was added to a large quantity of ethanol (b.pt. 78°C). The most probable boiling point of the resultant mixture is from
questions.explanation: Since ethanol is present in large excess, the mixture's boiling behaviour stays dominated by ethanol (78°C), only mildly depressed by the small amount of lower-boiling trichloromethane mixed in — so the boiling point sits just below pure ethanol's, in the 70°C–74°C range, rather than dropping all the way toward trichloromethane's 60°C or rising above ethanol's own boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The gas that gives brown colouration in brown ring test is
questions.explanation: The brown ring test for nitrates works because NO gas, released when a nitrate is treated with dilute acid and reduced by Fe2+, combines with excess Fe2+ ions to form the brown complex [Fe(NO)(H2O)5]2+ at the interface between the two liquid layers — it is specifically NO, not NO2, that forms this complex.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following gives a precipitate when treated with NaOH solution?
questions.explanation: AlCl3 reacts with NaOH to form a white gelatinous precipitate of Al(OH)3. NH4Cl with NaOH releases ammonia gas on warming but forms no precipitate. Na2CO3 and CH3COONa are both already soluble sodium salts that simply stay in solution with NaOH — no new insoluble product forms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of an alkene with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst is
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation of an alkene breaks the C=C pi bond and adds one hydrogen atom to each carbon, with nothing leaving the molecule — the defining feature of an addition reaction, catalysed typically by nickel or platinum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A rock sample was added to cold dilute HNO3. The gas evolved was passed into a solution of acidified K2Cr2O7 and the solution turned green. The rock sample contains
questions.explanation: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI) is an oxidising agent that turns from orange to green when it is reduced (Cr2O7^2- → Cr3+). Only a reducing gas can cause that colour change, and SO2 — released when dilute acid reacts with a sulphite (SO3^2-) — is exactly such a reducing gas. Sulphate (SO4^2-) releases no gas with dilute acid, nitrate needs concentrated acid or specific conditions to give a reducing gas, and chloride released as HCl gas is not a reducing agent toward dichromate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The intermediate product formed when ethanol is progressively oxidized to ethanoic acid with potassium heptaoxodichromate (VI) is
questions.explanation: Oxidation of a primary alcohol proceeds in two stages: alcohol → aldehyde → carboxylic acid, with each stage keeping the same carbon count. Ethanol (C2) is first oxidised to ethanal (C2 aldehyde) and then further to ethanoic acid (C2 acid) — the intermediate must have the same number of carbons as the starting alcohol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3 — the compound above is a
questions.explanation: The carbon bearing the -OH group is attached to two other carbon groups (a CH3 on one side and a CH2CH3 on the other) plus one hydrogen — that pattern, OH-carbon bonded to exactly two carbon chains, defines a secondary alcohol (this is butan-2-ol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A red precipitate of copper(I) carbide (acetylide) is formed when ammoniacal copper(I) chloride solution is introduced into
questions.explanation: Ammoniacal copper(I) chloride only gives a red precipitate with terminal alkynes — those with a hydrogen directly on a triple-bonded carbon (≡C-H), because that acidic hydrogen is replaced by copper to form the acetylide. But-2-yne has its triple bond in the middle with no acetylenic H, but-1-yne has a terminal ≡C-H, but-1-ene is an alkene (no triple bond at all), and butane is a saturated alkane with no multiple bond whatsoever.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The most important use of hydrogen is in the
questions.explanation: Hydrogen's single largest industrial use is the Haber process, combining it with nitrogen from the air to manufacture ammonia (N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3) — the foundation of the world's nitrogen fertiliser supply, which dwarfs hydrogen's other uses in scale.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following polymers is suitable for packaging and electrical insulation?
questions.explanation: Polyethene (polythene) is flexible, chemically inert, waterproof, and a good electrical insulator, making it the standard material for plastic packaging (bags, film, containers) and cable/wire insulation. Polystyrene is more associated with rigid/foam packaging and insulation panels rather than electrical wire insulation; polyamide (nylon) is mainly a textile/fibre polymer; polycarbonate is prized for impact-resistant transparency (e.g. lenses, CDs) rather than as a general packaging/insulation material.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The boiling of fat and aqueous caustic soda is referred to as
questions.explanation: Boiling a fat (an ester of glycerol and fatty acids) with concentrated aqueous NaOH is specifically called saponification — it hydrolyses the ester bonds under basic conditions to produce soap (sodium salts of fatty acids) and glycerol. 'Hydrolysis' is the broader chemical process happening, but the named process for fat + alkali specifically is saponification.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ordinary glass is manufactured from silica, CaCO3 and
questions.explanation: Ordinary soda-lime glass is made by fusing silica (sand, SiO2), limestone (CaCO3) and sodium carbonate (Na2CO3, 'soda ash') — the sodium carbonate lowers the melting point of silica, making large-scale glass production economical.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of isomers formed by C6H14 is
questions.explanation: C6H14 (hexane) has five structural isomers: n-hexane, 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane, and 2,3-dimethylbutane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of these pairs are synthetic and natural macromolecules respectively?
options: Nylon and polyethylene, keratin and haemoglobin
Nylon and keratin, polyethylene and haemoglobin
Polyethylene and keratin, nylon and haemoglobin
Haemoglobin and nylon, keratin and polyethylene
questions.explanation: Nylon and polyethylene are both man-made (synthetic) polymers, while keratin (in hair/nails) and haemoglobin (in blood) are both naturally occurring biological macromolecules — so the correct pairing keeps all synthetic examples together and all natural examples together.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An example of an element that can catenate is
questions.explanation: Catenation is the ability of atoms of the same element to bond to each other in long chains or rings. Carbon does this extensively (the basis of all organic chemistry), far more than nitrogen, chlorine, or bromine, which form at most very short chains under special conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethanol can easily be produced by
questions.explanation: The classic method of ethanol production is fermentation of starch/sugar solutions using yeast enzymes (starch is first hydrolysed to glucose, then fermented to ethanol and CO2) — this is the standard method taught and used industrially/traditionally.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hydrogen is readily released when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with
questions.explanation: Only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series displace it from dilute acids. Sodium is far more reactive than hydrogen and reacts vigorously with dilute HCl (and even with water) to release hydrogen gas. Silver, gold, and copper are all below hydrogen in reactivity and do not react with dilute HCl at all.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true of a proton?
options: The mass of a proton is 1.0008 g
The mass of a proton is negligible
The mass of a proton is about 1840 times the mass of an electron
The total mass of the protons in a particular nucleus is always half the nuclear mass
questions.explanation: A proton's mass is roughly 1840 times that of an electron — this ratio is the standard fact used to justify why electron mass is ignored in atomic mass calculations. Its actual mass is about 1.67×10^-24 g (not 1.0008 g, which is closer to its mass in atomic mass units, a different unit entirely), and it's the electron whose mass is comparatively negligible, not the proton's.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: A gas X diffuses twice as fast as gas Y under the same condition. If the relative molecular mass of X is 28, calculate the relative molecular mass of Y
questions.explanation: Graham's law: rate_X / rate_Y = √(My/Mx). Given rate_X = 2 × rate_Y: 2 = √(My/28), so My/28 = 4, giving My = 112.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following chlorides would exhibit the least ionic character?
questions.explanation: By Fajan's rules, ionic character decreases as the cation's charge increases and its size decreases, because a small, highly-charged cation polarises the electron cloud of the neighbouring chloride ion strongly, pulling shared electron density toward itself and giving the bond covalent character. Al3+ has the highest charge (+3) and a small ionic radius among these options, giving AlCl3 the strongest polarising power and therefore the least ionic (most covalent) character.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: A fixed mass of gas has a volume of 92 cm3 at 3°C. What will be its volume at 18°C if the pressure remains constant?
questions.explanation: Charles' law requires absolute temperature: T1 = 3 + 273 = 276 K, T2 = 18 + 273 = 291 K. V2 = V1 × (T2/T1) = 92 × (291/276) ≈ 97.0 cm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The processes which return carbon(IV) oxide to the atmosphere include
questions.explanation: Respiration, decay (decomposition of organic matter), and combustion (burning fuels) all release CO2 into the atmosphere. Photosynthesis does the opposite — it removes CO2 from the atmosphere to build plant biomass — so any option including photosynthesis as a 'return' process is incorrect, and ozone depletion is unrelated to the carbon cycle.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The postulate of Dalton's atomic theory which still holds is that
options: all elements are made of small indivisible particles
particles of different elements combine in a simple whole number ratio
atoms can neither be created nor destroyed
the particles of the same element are exactly alike
questions.explanation: Modern chemistry has disproved several of Dalton's original postulates: atoms ARE divisible (into protons, neutrons, electrons), and atoms of the same element are NOT all exactly alike (isotopes exist). What still holds, and remains a cornerstone of chemistry, is that atoms are neither created nor destroyed in ordinary chemical reactions — the basis of the law of conservation of mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: If 0.75 mole of cyclopropane and 0.66 mole of oxygen are mixed in a vessel with a total pressure of 0.7 atmosphere, what is the partial pressure of oxygen in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure. Total moles = 0.75 + 0.66 = 1.41. Mole fraction of O2 = 0.66/1.41 ≈ 0.468. Partial pressure of O2 = 0.468 × 0.7 ≈ 0.33 atm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When H2S is passed into a solution of iron(III) chloride, the solution turns
questions.explanation: H2S is a reducing agent and reduces yellow/brown Fe3+ to pale green Fe2+, while itself being oxidised to a pale precipitate of sulphur (giving the solution a cloudy pale-green/yellow appearance overall, but the characteristic colour change described is toward pale green from the Fe2+ formed).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cu2S(s) + O2(g) → 2Cu(s) + SO2(g). What is the change in the oxidation number of copper in the reaction above?
questions.explanation: In Cu2S, sulfur (more electronegative) is assigned -2, so the two copper atoms together must total +2, giving each Cu an oxidation state of +1. In the product, copper appears as the free element Cu(s), which by definition has an oxidation state of 0. So copper's oxidation number changes from +1 to 0 — a reduction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction E + F ⇌ G + H, the backward reaction is favoured if the concentration of
questions.explanation: The backward reaction (G + H → E + F) is favoured when the system shifts to replace something that's been removed from the reactant side. If E's concentration is reduced, Le Chatelier's principle predicts the equilibrium shifts to produce more E — meaning the backward reaction is favoured to replenish it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The products of the electrolysis of dilute sodium hydroxide using platinum electrodes are
questions.explanation: In dilute aqueous NaOH, water is preferentially discharged at both electrodes rather than Na+ (too reactive to be discharged in aqueous solution) or OH- directly as a separate product — hydrogen gas forms at the cathode and oxygen gas forms at the anode, essentially electrolysing the water while the NaOH concentration in solution slowly increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: PCl5(g) ⇌ PCl3(g) + Cl2(g). In the reaction above, a decrease in pressure will
questions.explanation: The forward reaction produces 2 moles of gas from 1 mole, increasing the total number of gas particles. By Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing pressure favours the side with more gas moles — so the equilibrium shifts forward, increasing PCl3 (and Cl2) yield.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Arrhenius equation expresses the relationship between the speed of a reaction and its
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation (k = A·e^(-Ea/RT)) mathematically relates the rate constant k to temperature and the activation energy Ea — it's specifically the quantitative link between reaction rate and activation energy (and temperature).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What amount of mercury would be liberated if the same quantity of electricity that liberated 0.65 g of zinc is supplied? [Zn = 65, Hg = 201]
questions.explanation: Moles of Zn = 0.65/65 = 0.01 mol. Since Zn2+ needs 2 electrons per ion, total charge passed = 0.01 × 2 = 0.02 mol of electrons. For Hg2+ (also needing 2 electrons per ion), moles of Hg deposited = 0.02/2 = 0.01 mol. Mass of Hg = 0.01 × 201 = 2.01 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When dissolved in water, NaOH flakes show
questions.explanation: Dissolving NaOH in water is a strongly exothermic process — the container noticeably heats up as the solid dissolves, a well-known and commonly demonstrated property of sodium hydroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Steam changes the colour of anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride from
questions.explanation: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride is blue; when it absorbs water (as from steam), it turns pink as it becomes hydrated (CoCl2·6H2O) — this colour change is the standard test used to detect the presence of water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The solubility of a salt of molar mass 101 g at 20°C is 0.34 mol dm⁻³. If 3.40 g of the salt is dissolved completely in 250 cm3 of water in a beaker, the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: Moles dissolved = 3.40/101 ≈ 0.0337 mol. Concentration = 0.0337 mol / 0.250 dm3 ≈ 0.135 mol dm⁻³. Since this (0.135) is well below the solubility limit (0.34 mol dm⁻³), more salt could still dissolve — the solution is unsaturated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 25 cm3 of a 0.2 mol dm⁻³ solution of Na2CO3 requires 20 cm3 of a solution of HCl for neutralization. The concentration of the HCl solution is
questions.explanation: Na2CO3 + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H2O + CO2, so 1 mole of Na2CO3 needs 2 moles of HCl. Moles Na2CO3 = 0.025 dm3 × 0.2 mol/dm3 = 0.005 mol, requiring 0.01 mol HCl. Concentration of HCl = 0.01 mol / 0.020 dm3 = 0.5 mol dm⁻³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When a salt loses its water of crystallization to the atmosphere on exposure, the process is said to be
questions.explanation: Efflorescence is specifically the loss of water of crystallization from a hydrated salt to the surrounding air, often leaving a powdery residue. Effervescence refers to bubbling/gas release, fluorescence is a light-emission phenomenon, and deliquescence is the opposite process — a substance absorbing so much moisture from the air that it dissolves itself.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Three drops of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ solution of NaOH are added to 20 cm3 of a solution of pH 8.4. The pH of the resulting solution will be
options: close to that of pure water
questions.explanation: Adding a strong base (NaOH) to any solution increases its hydroxide ion concentration, pushing the pH upward — so even a small addition raises the pH above the original 8.4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid burns the skin by
questions.explanation: Concentrated sulphuric acid (tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid) has a powerful affinity for water and rips hydrogen and oxygen atoms out of organic tissue in the ratio found in water, charring it — this is dehydration, the same effect seen when it chars sugar or paper.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The substance least considered as a source of environmental pollution is
questions.explanation: Uranium (radioactive contamination), lead compounds (heavy metal toxicity), and organophosphorus compounds (pesticide toxicity) are all well-known, actively-cited environmental and health hazards. Silicate minerals, by contrast, are common, largely chemically inert natural rock/soil components and are not typically classified as pollutants.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The property which makes alcohol soluble in water is the
questions.explanation: Alcohols dissolve readily in water because their -OH group can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, just as water molecules hydrogen-bond with each other — this specific intermolecular attraction is what allows the two very different-looking substances to mix freely.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The furring of kettles is caused by the presence in water of
questions.explanation: Temporary hardness in water is caused by dissolved calcium hydrogencarbonate (Ca(HCO3)2), which is soluble. On boiling, it decomposes to insoluble calcium carbonate (CaCO3), releasing CO2 and water — that insoluble CaCO3 is the 'fur'/scale that deposits inside kettles. The question asks what's present IN the water beforehand, which is the soluble bicarbonate, not the insoluble carbonate that forms afterward.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What volume of oxygen is produced from the decomposition of 2 moles of KClO3 at s.t.p? [Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm3]
questions.explanation: 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2. The mole ratio of KClO3 to O2 is 2:3, so 2 moles of KClO3 produce 3 moles of O2. Volume = 3 × 22.4 dm3 = 67.2 dm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the percentage by mass of oxygen in Al2(SO4)3.2H2O? [Al = 27, S = 32, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass: Al2(SO4)3 = 2(27) + 3(32+64) = 54 + 288 = 342. Add 2H2O = 2(18) = 36. Total = 378 g/mol. Oxygen atoms: 12 from the three sulfate groups + 2 from the two water molecules = 14 oxygen atoms, mass = 14×16 = 224 g. Percentage O = 224/378 × 100 ≈ 59.25%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The filter in a cigarette reduces the nicotine content by
questions.explanation: Cigarette filters (often containing activated carbon or cellulose acetate fibres) trap nicotine molecules on their surface — this surface-trapping process is specifically called adsorption, distinct from absorption (which means being taken up into the bulk of a material).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 3Cu + pHNO3 → 3Cu(NO3)2 + 4H2O + xNO. In the equation above, the values of p and x respectively are
questions.explanation: Balance hydrogen first: the right side has 4H2O = 8 H atoms, so p (HNO3 coefficient) must be 8 to supply 8 H atoms. Check nitrogen: left side has p = 8 N atoms; right side has 3×2 = 6 N atoms in Cu(NO3)2 plus x in NO, so 8 = 6 + x, giving x = 2. Both values check out: p = 8, x = 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The noble gases owe their inactivity to
questions.explanation: Noble gases (except helium) have a complete octet of 8 electrons in their outermost shell, an especially stable arrangement that gives them very little tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons — hence their chemical inactivity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: According to the kinetic theory, an increase in temperature causes the kinetic energy of particles to
questions.explanation: Kinetic theory directly links temperature to the average kinetic energy of particles — as temperature rises, particles move faster on average, meaning their average kinetic energy increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: A gas exerts pressure on its container because
options: some of its molecules are moving faster than others
of the collision of the molecules with each other
of the mass of the molecules of gas
the molecules of a gas collide with the walls of the container
questions.explanation: Gas pressure arises specifically from gas molecules continually colliding with and rebounding off the container walls, transferring momentum at each collision. Molecule-to-molecule collisions, varying speeds, and molecular mass alone don't directly explain what pressure IS — they're related but distinct aspects of kinetic theory.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When cathode rays are deflected onto the electrode of an electrometer, the instrument becomes
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons — negatively charged particles. When they strike and accumulate on the electrometer's electrode, they deposit negative charge onto it, making the instrument negatively charged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The weakest attractive forces that can be observed between two molecules is
questions.explanation: Van der Waals forces are weak, temporary attractions arising from fluctuating electron distributions between molecules — much weaker than the strong chemical bonds (ionic, covalent, coordinate covalent) that hold atoms together within a molecule or compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A consequence of global warming is
questions.explanation: Global warming raises sea levels (through thermal expansion and melting polar ice) and intensifies extreme weather, both of which directly increase the risk and severity of flooding — a well-established and commonly cited direct consequence.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following ions is acidic?
questions.explanation: H3O+ (the hydronium ion) is, by definition, the species responsible for acidity in aqueous solution — its presence and concentration directly determine how acidic a solution is. K+ and NO3- are spectator ions from a neutral salt (KNO3), and S2- is actually basic (it's the conjugate base of a weak acid, H2S).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The structural component that makes detergent dissolve more quickly in water than soap is
questions.explanation: Synthetic detergents typically use a sulfonate head group (-SO3-Na+), which stays fully soluble even in hard water (doesn't form insoluble precipitates with Ca2+/Mg2+ the way soap's carboxylate group does), giving detergents faster, more reliable dissolution and cleaning action. Soap's characteristic group is the carboxylate (-COO-Na+ or -COO-K+), which is the group that forms scum in hard water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A liquid that will dissolve fat is
questions.explanation: Fats are non-polar substances, so 'like dissolves like' — they dissolve readily in non-polar organic solvents such as kerosene, but not in polar substances like water, dilute HCl, or aqueous calcium hydroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Farmlands affected by crude-oil spillage can be decontaminated by
options: pouring water on the affected area
burning off the oil from the area
questions.explanation: Bioremediation — using aerobic bacteria that metabolise hydrocarbons — is the standard method for decontaminating oil-affected soil, breaking the oil down into less harmful substances without the further environmental damage caused by burning or simply adding water/acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A change in the temperature of a saturated solution disturbs the equilibrium between the
options: dissolved solute and the undissolved solute
questions.explanation: In a saturated solution, there's a dynamic equilibrium between solute already dissolved and any excess (undissolved) solute — the rate of dissolving equals the rate of recrystallising. Changing temperature shifts where that balance sits, since solubility itself is temperature-dependent, disturbing precisely this dissolved/undissolved equilibrium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If an equilibrium reaction has ΔH > 0, the reaction will proceed favourably in the forward direction at
questions.explanation: ΔH > 0 means the forward reaction is endothermic (absorbs heat). By Le Chatelier's principle, adding heat (raising temperature) shifts an endothermic equilibrium further forward, since the system responds to the added heat by consuming it via the forward reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The commonest feature of reaction at the anode is that
questions.explanation: By definition, the anode is where oxidation occurs — species lose electrons there, whether in electrolytic or galvanic cells. This is a universal feature of anode reactions, unlike the other listed options, which don't consistently apply across all anode reactions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following will change when a catalyst is added to a chemical reaction?
options: The potential energy of the reactants
The potential energy of the products
questions.explanation: A catalyst works by providing an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy, speeding up the reaction without being consumed. It does NOT change the potential energy of the reactants or products, and it does not change the overall heat of reaction (ΔH) — those are fixed by the identities of reactants and products, independent of the pathway taken.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If Y is an oxidizing agent that reacts with a reducing agent, Z, which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: By definition, an oxidizing agent is itself reduced during the reaction (it gains electrons, its oxidation number decreases) while causing the other species (the reducing agent) to be oxidised. So Y, the oxidizing agent, becomes reduced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When at equilibrium, which of the reactions below will shift to the right if the pressure is increased and the temperature is kept constant?
questions.explanation: Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium toward the side with fewer moles of gas. Only 2H2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2H2O(g) has fewer gas moles on the product (right) side — 3 moles of reactant gas becoming 2 moles of product gas — so increased pressure shifts it to the right. The other reactions either have more moles on the product side (shifting left instead) or equal moles on both sides (no pressure effect).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the electrolysis of a concentrated solution of sodium chloride using inert electrodes, which of the following ions are discharged at the cathode and anode respectively?
questions.explanation: At the cathode, Na+ is too reactive to be discharged in aqueous solution, so H+ (from water) is preferentially reduced to H2 gas instead. At the anode, although OH- is normally preferentially discharged over Cl- in dilute solution, at high (concentrated) chloride concentration, Cl- is discharged instead, producing Cl2 gas — this is the industrially important chlor-alkali process.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When sugar is dissolved in tea, the reaction is always accompanied by
questions.explanation: Dissolving a solid (sugar, an ordered crystal lattice) into a liquid disperses its particles randomly throughout the solution, increasing the overall disorder of the system — this increase in disorder is a positive entropy change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is an electrolyte?
questions.explanation: An electrolyte is a substance that conducts electricity via ion movement when dissolved or molten. Sodium acetate SOLUTION has mobile dissociated ions and conducts electricity — a true electrolyte. Alcohol is molecular and doesn't ionise. Solid KOH has ions locked in a rigid lattice (not mobile) so it doesn't conduct until dissolved or molten. Mercury conducts via free electrons (metallic conduction), not via ions, so it isn't classified as an electrolyte.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine gas is prepared in the laboratory by
options: adding concentrated hydrochloric acid to solid manganese(IV) oxide
adding concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid to solid sodium chloride
dropping concentrated hydrochloric acid onto potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) crystals
oxidizing concentrated hydrochloric acid using potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI) crystals
questions.explanation: The standard laboratory preparation of chlorine, as emphasised in the syllabus, is MnO2(s) + 4HCl(conc) → MnCl2 + Cl2 + 2H2O (with gentle heating) — manganese(IV) oxide oxidising concentrated hydrochloric acid to release chlorine gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Metals of the transition series have special properties which are different from those of groups 1 and 11 elements because they have partially filled
questions.explanation: Transition metals are specifically defined by having partially filled d orbitals (or forming ions with partially filled d orbitals), which is the source of their characteristic properties: variable oxidation states, coloured compounds, and catalytic activity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hydrogen can be displaced from a hot alkaline solution by
questions.explanation: Tin is amphoteric — it reacts with both acids and hot concentrated alkalis, releasing hydrogen gas as it forms a stannate ion in the alkaline solution. Iron and copper don't react with alkaline solutions this way, and calcium's reactivity is characteristically with water/acids rather than being noted for this specific amphoteric alkali reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true of sulphur(IV) oxide?
options: It forms tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid with water
It forms a white precipitate with acidified barium chloride
questions.explanation: Sulphur(IV) oxide (SO2) is the acid anhydride of sulphurous acid (tetraoxosulphate(IV) acid, H2SO3) — it forms H2SO3, not H2SO4, when dissolved in water. It has a sharp, pungent (not odourless) smell, and being an unoxidised sulphite in solution, it does not give the white BaSO4 precipitate with acidified barium chloride the way a true sulphate does.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The salt that will form a precipitate soluble in excess ammonia solution is
questions.explanation: Cu(NO3)2 forms a pale blue Cu(OH)2 precipitate with ammonia, which then DISSOLVES in excess ammonia to form the deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex, [Cu(NH3)4]2+ — a classic distinguishing test. Ca(NO3)2 doesn't reliably form a precipitate with ammonia; Mg(OH)2 and Al(OH)3 precipitates both form but stay insoluble even in excess ammonia.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The metal that liberates hydrogen from cold water in bubbles only is
questions.explanation: Calcium reacts with cold water at a controlled, steady rate, producing a visible stream of hydrogen bubbles without the violent, often flame-producing reaction seen with sodium and potassium. Aluminium, by contrast, does not react with cold water at all under normal conditions, protected by its tough oxide layer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine gas turns a damp starch-iodide paper
questions.explanation: Chlorine is a strong enough oxidising agent to displace iodine from iodide ions on the paper (Cl2 + 2I- → 2Cl- + I2). The liberated iodine then forms its characteristic deep blue-black complex with the starch present on the paper.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The modern process of manufacturing steel from iron is by
questions.explanation: Converting iron (pig iron, containing excess carbon and other impurities from the blast furnace) into steel involves blowing oxygen through the molten iron to oxidise and remove the excess carbon and impurities — this is fundamentally an oxidation process (e.g. the Basic Oxygen Process).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethene reacts with hydrogen bromide to give
questions.explanation: HBr adds across ethene's C=C double bond in a simple addition reaction: CH2=CH2 + HBr → CH3CH2Br (bromoethane). Only one H and one Br are added, one to each carbon, with no other change to the molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Carbohydrates are compounds containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y, meaning for every carbon atom there are 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom — a C:H:O ratio of 1:2:1, reflecting that they're literally 'hydrates of carbon'.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many isomers does pentane have?
questions.explanation: C5H12 (pentane) has exactly three structural isomers: n-pentane (straight chain), 2-methylbutane (isopentane), and 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The formula for ethyl butanoate is
questions.explanation: Ester naming follows 'alkyl alkanoate': the alkyl part (ethyl, C2H5) comes from the alcohol, and the alkanoate part (butanoate, from butanoic acid, C3H7COOH) comes from the acid. So ethyl butanoate = C3H7COO-C2H5, with the acid's carbon chain (C3H7-COO-) written first and the alcohol's alkyl group (ethyl) second.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The type of reaction that is peculiar to benzene is
questions.explanation: Despite benzene's ring containing what looks like alternating double bonds, its special aromatic stability (delocalised pi electron system) makes it resistant to the addition reactions typical of alkenes — instead, benzene characteristically undergoes electrophilic substitution, preserving its stable ring while swapping out a hydrogen for another group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethanol reacts with excess acidified K2Cr2O7 to give
questions.explanation: With EXCESS acidified dichromate (a strong, plentiful oxidising agent), ethanol is fully oxidised all the way through the aldehyde intermediate (ethanal) to the carboxylic acid — ethanoic acid — the final oxidation product for a primary alcohol under these conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen. If the molar mass of the compound is 180, find the molecular formula. [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Empirical formula: C = 40/12 = 3.33; H = 6.7/1 = 6.7; O = 53.3/16 = 3.33. Dividing by the smallest (3.33) gives a ratio of 1 : 2.01 : 1, i.e. CH2O (empirical formula mass = 30). Since molar mass = 180, the multiplier n = 180/30 = 6, giving molecular formula C6H12O6 (glucose).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The process by which atoms are rearranged into different molecular structures in the petroleum refining process is referred to as
questions.explanation: Reforming rearranges the structure of hydrocarbon molecules (e.g. converting straight-chain alkanes into branched or aromatic ones) without necessarily changing their size — improving fuel quality (like octane rating) through structural rearrangement, distinct from cracking (which breaks molecules into smaller ones) or polymerization (which joins molecules into larger ones).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is found in cotton?
questions.explanation: Cotton fibres are composed almost entirely of cellulose, a structural polysaccharide that gives plant cell walls (and cotton fibres specifically) their strength and fibrous character.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following equimolar solutions will have the highest pH?
questions.explanation: To solve this, you need to remember that the pH scale runs from 0 to 14. A 'high pH' means the solution is very basic. Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH) is a strong base, meaning it dissociates completely in water to release a maximum amount of hydroxide ions (OH-). While NH4OH is also a base, it's a weak one, so it won't push the pH as high as NaOH will for the same concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following ions require the largest quantity of electricity for discharge at an electrode?
questions.explanation: The quantity of electricity (Q) depends on both the number of moles and the charge (valency) of the ion: Q = n x z x F. A (4x1=4F), B (3x1=3F), C (2.5x2=5F), D (2.0x3=6F). Even though Aluminum has the fewest moles, its +3 charge means it needs more electricity per atom to discharge, making it the winner with 6 Faradays.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Phenolphthalein in acidic solution is
questions.explanation: Indicators are substances that change colour depending on the acidity of a solution. Phenolphthalein is a very common indicator that stays completely clear (colourless) in acids but turns a bright pink or red in basic (alkaline) solutions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When iron is exposed to moisture and it rusts, the value of ΔG for the reaction is
questions.explanation: The trick here is to identify if the process is spontaneous. Since iron rusts by itself when left in moisture, it is spontaneous. For any spontaneous process, the Gibbs Free Energy change (ΔG) must be negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name for NO2-?
questions.explanation: Number of oxygens: 2 means dioxo. Oxidation state of N: x+2(-2)=-1, so x=+3. Name: Dioxonitrate (III). Nitrate (V) would be NO3-.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many moles of limestone (CaCO3) will be required to produce 5.6g of CaO? [Ca = 40, C = 12, O= 16]
questions.explanation: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2, a 1:1 ratio. Molar mass of CaO = 40+16=56g/mol. 5.6/56 = 0.1 moles CaO, so 0.1 moles CaCO3 needed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The property used in the industrial preparation of nitrogen and oxygen from air is
questions.explanation: Air is liquefied and undergoes fractional distillation. Nitrogen boils at -196C and Oxygen at -183C, allowing separate collection. Fractional distillation = boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following alloys contain iron?
questions.explanation: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon. Permalloy is a magnetic alloy of iron and nickel. Duralumin is Aluminum-based; Brass and Bronze are copper-based.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The raw materials used for the smelting of iron ore in a furnace is
questions.explanation: Blast furnace needs coke, hot air, and limestone (CaCO3). Limestone decomposes to CaO which reacts with silica impurities to form slag.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: H2(g) + Br2(g) -> 2HBr(g). The above reaction is carried out at 25C. ΔH is -72 kJ mol-1 and ΔS is -106 J mol-1K-1. The reaction will?
options: not proceed spontaneously at the given temperature
proceed spontaneously at the given temperature
proceed in the reverse direction at the given temperature
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS (convert ΔS to kJ). ΔG = -72 - (298 x -0.106) = -72+31.588 = -40.412 kJ. Negative ΔG means spontaneous at this temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: One mole of a hydrocarbon contains 36g of carbon and its vapour density is 20. The structure of the hydrocarbon is
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 2 x VD = 40g/mol. Carbon: 36/12=3 atoms. Remaining mass 4g = 4 H atoms. Formula C3H4 = Propyne (CH3C≡CH).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When 50cm3 of a saturated solution of sugar of molar mass 342g at 40C was evaporated to dryness, 34.2g of dry solid was obtained. The solubility of sugar at 40C is
questions.explanation: Moles of sugar = 34.2/342 = 0.1 mol in 50cm3. Scale to 1000cm3: (0.1x1000)/50 = 2.0 mol/dm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 5SO2(g) + 2KMnO4(aq) + 2H2O(l) -> K2SO4 + 2MnSO4(aq) + 2H2SO4(aq). In the reaction above, the products give a
questions.explanation: KMnO4 is purple due to MnO4-. SO2 reduces Mn from +7 (purple) to +2 (Mn2+, colourless). All products soluble, so result is a clear colourless solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following functional groups will give gas bubbles when treated with a saturated solution of sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate (IV)?
questions.explanation: Only acids are strong enough to displace CO2 from NaHCO3. The -COOH group (carboxylic acids) reacts with NaHCO3 to give a salt, water, and effervescence of CO2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Trioxonitrate (V) acid is not used for preparing hydrogen gas from metals because it
options: forms a layer of oxide on the metal
questions.explanation: HNO3 is a powerful oxidizing agent. As soon as hydrogen forms, the acid oxidizes it to water, and the acid is reduced to nitrogen oxides. Result: water and brown fumes, not H2 gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An element used in the production of matches is
questions.explanation: Match heads contain sulphur as a fuel plus oxidizing agents like potassium chlorate. Red phosphorus is on the striking surface, but sulphur is the element from this list in the match industry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How long would it take to deposit 0.08g of copper from CuCl2 solution by passing a current of 0.5A? [Cu = 64, 1F = 96500 C mol-1]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound CH3CH2COOCH2CH3 is
questions.explanation: Alcohol side: -CH2CH3 = ethyl. Acid side (3 carbons incl. carbonyl): CH3-CH2-CO- = propanoate. Together: ethyl propanoate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many electrons are in the L shell of 31/15 P?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 15. Configuration: 2(K), 8(L), 5(M). L shell has 8 electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What weight of NaCl is needed to make 2.0 dm3 of a 1.5M solution? [Na = 23, Cl = 35.5]
questions.explanation: Moles = 1.5 x 2.0 = 3.0 moles. Molar mass NaCl = 58.5g/mol. Mass = 3.0 x 58.5 = 175.5g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorophyll obtained from green leaves of plant can be shown to be composed of more than one coloured component by the technique of
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates components of a mixture based on their different rates of movement across a material (like paper). Whenever you see a question about separating colours, pigments, or ink, chromatography should be your first thought.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In countries where the temperature falls below 273K, salt is always sprinkled on the icy road in order to
options: lower the melting point of the ice
increase the density of the ice
raise the melting point of the ice
questions.explanation: Freezing point depression: pure water freezes at 273K. Adding salt (impurity) interferes with ice crystal formation, lowering the freezing point so ice melts even in cold weather.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 2Na(s) + 2H2O(l) -> 2NaOH(aq) + H2(g). From the equation above, calculate the mass of sodium hydroxide produced by 2.3g of sodium. [H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23]
questions.explanation: Na=23, NaOH=40. 2 mol Na(46g) produces 2 mol NaOH(80g). 2.3g Na is 1/20 of 46g, so mass NaOH = 80/20 = 4.0g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: 300 cm3 of gas has a pressure of 800 mmHg. If the pressure is reduced to 650 mmHg, find its volume

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the pH of 0.001 mol dm-3 solution of sodium hydroxide?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A mixture of sugar and sulphur can be separated by
options: dissolution in water, evaporation and filtration
filtration, evaporation and dissolution in water
dissolution in water, filtration and evaporation
evaporation, dissolution in water and filtration
questions.explanation: Sugar dissolves in water, sulphur doesn't. Dissolve, filter out insoluble sulphur, then evaporate the filtrate to recover sugar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The percentage of water of crystallization in ZnSO4.7H2O is? [Zn = 65, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 0.0075 mole of calcium trioxocarbonate (IV) is added to 0.015 mole of a solution of hydrochloric acid. The volume of gas evolved at s.t.p is? [Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm3]
questions.explanation: CaCO3+2HCl->CaCl2+H2O+CO2, ratio 1:2. 0.0075 mol CaCO3 exactly matches 0.015 mol HCl. CO2 = 0.0075mol x 22.4 = 0.168dm3 = 168cm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which quantum number divides shells into orbitals?
questions.explanation: Principal quantum number (n) gives the shell. Azimuthal (l) breaks shells into sub-shells/orbitals (s,p,d,f).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The salt formed from a reaction between citric acid and sodium hydroxide in solution will be
questions.explanation: NaOH is a strong base, citric acid is a weak acid. Strong base wins the pH battle, giving a basic salt.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following metals is purified commercially by electrolysis?
questions.explanation: Copper is famously purified by electrolysis: impure copper anode, pure copper cathode, electrical energy moves pure copper to the cathode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The simplest branched-chain hydrocarbon is
questions.explanation: A branch needs at least 4 carbons. 2-methylpropane (isobutane) has 4 carbons with a center carbon attached to three others — the smallest branched molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in calcium trioxonitrate (V) [Ca = 40, N = 14, O = 16]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: The volume of a given gas is V cm3 at a pressure P mm Hg. What is the new volume of the gas if the pressure is reduced to half at constant temperature?
questions.explanation: P1V1=P2V2. Halving pressure means volume must double: 2V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Calculate the volume of 0.5 mol dm-3 H2SO4 that is neutralized by 25 cm3 of 0.1 mol dm-3 NaOH?
questions.explanation: H2SO4+2NaOH->Na2SO4+2H2O, ratio na=1,nb=2. CaVa/na=CbVb/nb: 0.5Va/1=(0.1x25)/2=1.25. Va=2.5cm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of increasing boiling points of the following compounds C3H7OH, C7H16 and C4H10 is?
questions.explanation: Propanol has hydrogen bonding, giving it the highest boiling point. Between the alkanes, the longer chain (C7) has more Van der Waals forces than the shorter (C4). Order: C4 < C7 < alcohol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: On heating, which of the following compounds will decompose to the free metal, nitrogen(IV) oxide and oxygen?
questions.explanation: The trick here is knowing that not all nitrates decompose the same way when heated - it depends on where the metal sits on the reactivity series. Very reactive metals (Na, K) only lose oxygen, giving the nitrite. Moderately reactive metals (Mg up to Cu) break down to the metal oxide plus NO2 and O2. But metals low on the reactivity series - like silver - are so unstable as compounds that heat pushes all the way down to the free metal itself. That's why 2AgNO3 -> 2Ag + 2NO2 + O2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The group IA metals are not found free in nature because they
options: have high melting and boiling point
questions.explanation: An element only exists free (uncombined) in nature if it's unreactive enough to survive on its own - think gold, or the noble gases. Alkali metals are the opposite: they react violently with water, and even just moisture or oxygen in the air, so they instantly form compounds. That's why you'll never dig up a lump of pure sodium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Carbon exists naturally in the combined state as
questions.explanation: Don't rush - 'combined' has a specific meaning here: carbon chemically bonded to other elements, forming a compound. Graphite, diamond, and coal are all classed as forms of free (elemental) carbon - just pure carbon atoms arranged differently, or carbon with impurities. Wood is different: it's mostly cellulose, where carbon is genuinely bonded to hydrogen and oxygen in a real compound. That makes wood the true example of carbon in the combined state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The efficiency of a solid catalyst to increase reaction rates depends on its
questions.explanation: A solid catalyst speeds up a reaction by giving reactant molecules a surface to land on and react at (active sites). The more surface exposed, the more of these active sites are available at once - which is exactly why catalysts are often used as fine powders, pellets, or mesh rather than solid lumps.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Dynamic equilibrium describes a situation where
options: a reaction gives back the reactant
the concentration of the reactant and products is equal
both forward and reverse reactions proceed at the same rate
questions.explanation: The word 'dynamic' is the giveaway - the reaction hasn't stopped, both directions are still happening, just at matching speeds. So concentrations stay constant not because nothing's moving, but because whatever forms is being used up again just as fast.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The ion that will give a white precipitate with aqueous NaOH and is soluble in excess of the base is
questions.explanation: This is where students usually get caught mixing up two separate tests: the colour of the precipitate, and whether it redissolves in excess. Zn(OH)2 forms white and is amphoteric - it dissolves back into excess NaOH to form a soluble zincate ion. That combination (white AND redissolves) is what makes zinc unique among these four.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The characteristic colour of the flame shown when a copper salt moistened with concentrated hydrochloric acid on a platinum wire is put on a Bunsen burner is
questions.explanation: This is pure recall, so it's worth locking the flame colours in as a set: copper gives green (sometimes described as blue-green), potassium gives lilac, sodium gives yellow, and calcium gives brick-red.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the industrial production of H2 from natural gas, the CO2 produced along with the H2 is removed by
options: passing the mixture into lime water
questions.explanation: This is where students usually mix up a lab TEST with an industrial PROCESS. Lime water genuinely does react with CO2 - but that's a small-scale identification test, not something you can run continuously on a huge industrial gas stream. On a plant scale, CO2 is scrubbed out economically by washing the gas mixture under pressure. Same target gas, very different scale of solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The sulphide which is insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid is
