questions.explanation: Don't assume all metal sulphides behave the same way with acid - it depends on how tightly the metal holds onto the sulphide ion. FeS and ZnS dissolve readily in dilute HCl (this is actually how H2S gas is made in the lab). But CuS has such a low solubility, its structure resists dilute acid entirely - you'd need concentrated nitric acid to break it down.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following typically represents a photochemical reaction?
options: Formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen molecules
Conversion of dinitrogen(IV) oxide to nitrogen(IV) oxide
Decomposition of calcium hydroxide to its oxide
Conversion of silver halides to grey metallic silver
questions.explanation: A photochemical reaction is specifically one driven by light energy, not heat or a spark. The classic textbook example is photographic film: silver halide crystals (like AgBr) turn into grey metallic silver the moment light hits them - that's literally how old-style photography captured an image.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The gas obtained as a product of anaerobic action on organic matter buried in the earth is
questions.explanation: Anaerobic just means 'without oxygen' - and when bacteria break down buried organic matter with no oxygen around, the gas they release is methane (sometimes called 'marsh gas' or biogas). This is the same process, over geological time, that builds up natural gas deposits underground.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Nigerian crude oil is described as light crude because of its
questions.explanation: Nigerian crude is famous on the world market as 'light, sweet' crude - light referring to its lower density, sweet referring to its low sulphur content. These two traits go hand in hand, which is why the exam key ties the 'light' description to low sulphur: it means the oil needs less processing to strip out impurities, making it more valuable to refiners.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An example of an aliphatic unsaturated hydrocarbon is
questions.explanation: You need both boxes ticked here: aliphatic means an open chain (not a ring), and unsaturated means it has a C=C or C≡C bond. Propene is a straight-chain alkene - it satisfies both conditions at once.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An emulsion may be produced by shaking a detergent solution with
questions.explanation: An emulsion needs two liquids that don't normally mix, with a third substance (here, the detergent) stabilizing tiny droplets of one dispersed through the other. Palm oil and water don't mix on their own - shaking them with detergent creates that fine dispersion. Palm wine, ethanoic acid, and water are all miscible with water already, so there's no separate phase to disperse in the first place.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The products of the combustion of candle wax are
questions.explanation: Candle wax is a hydrocarbon, so the default rule applies: complete combustion of any hydrocarbon in plenty of oxygen gives carbon(IV) oxide and water as the only products.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A decrease in atomic size and an increase in nuclear charge across a period lead to
options: an increase in the tendency to lose electron
a decrease in covalency in bond formation
questions.explanation: Picture what's happening physically: as you move across a period, more protons pull the same outer shell in tighter, so electrons are held more firmly. That makes it harder, not easier, to lose an electron - which is exactly what a decrease in electropositivity means (moving away from 'metal-like' behaviour toward non-metal behaviour).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The order in which a mixture of sand, ammonium chloride and sodium chloride can be separated is
questions.explanation: Walk through it one property at a time. Ammonium chloride is the odd one out because it sublimes on heating - so heat the dry mixture first and let it escape, leaving sand and sodium chloride behind. Then dissolve that residue in water: sodium chloride dissolves, sand doesn't. Filter to pull out the insoluble sand. Finally, evaporate the filtrate to recover solid sodium chloride. Each step targets exactly one property, in the order it becomes useful: sublimation → dissolution → filtration → evaporation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The idea of planetary electron was that of
questions.explanation: This is where students often get caught, because Bohr's diagrams look similar. But the 'planetary model' - electrons circling a tiny, dense nucleus the way planets orbit the sun - comes from Rutherford's 1911 gold-foil scattering experiment. Bohr came afterward and refined it by adding fixed, quantized energy levels; that refinement is Bohr's specific contribution, but the original planetary picture belongs to Rutherford.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Na2CO3(aq) + 2HCl(aq) -> 2NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g). What is the concentration of a sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) solution, 25 cm3 of which is exactly neutralized by 10 cm3 of 0.05 mol dm-3 hydrochloric acid solution?
questions.explanation: Before touching a calculator, notice this is really a mole-ratio problem in disguise. Moles of HCl used = 0.010 dm3 x 0.05 mol dm-3 = 0.0005 mol. The equation shows 2 mol HCl reacts with every 1 mol Na2CO3, so moles of Na2CO3 = 0.0005 / 2 = 0.00025 mol. That's the amount present in the 25 cm3 (0.025 dm3) sample, so concentration = 0.00025 / 0.025 = 0.010 mol dm-3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the electrolysis of brine, the anode is
questions.explanation: The trick here is remembering that an anode in this kind of electrolysis must be inert - it shouldn't react with the electrolyte or interfere with the products. Carbon (graphite) fits perfectly: it won't dissolve, and it lets chlorine gas be discharged cleanly at the anode. That's why graphite electrodes were the traditional choice in industrial brine electrolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g). In the endothermic reaction above, more product formation will be favoured by
questions.explanation: Count the moles of gas on each side before touching Le Chatelier's principle: 1 mole of N2O4 makes 2 moles of NO2, so the product side has more gas particles. Lowering the pressure gives the system 'room to expand', and it responds by shifting toward the side with more moles - the product side. So decreasing pressure favours more NO2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following hydrogen halides has the highest entropy value?
questions.explanation: Entropy is really a measure of disorder and the number of ways energy can be spread out. Heavier, larger molecules have more electrons and more accessible vibrational/rotational states, so their entropy tends to be higher. Among the hydrogen halides, HI has the largest, heaviest halogen atom, giving it the highest standard molar entropy of the group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The mass of silver deposited when a current of 10A is passed through a solution of silver salt for 4830s. [Ag = 108, F = 96500 C mol-1]
questions.explanation: Work through this in two clean stages rather than jumping straight to mass. First, find the charge passed: Q = I x t = 10A x 4830s = 48,300 C. Next, convert that charge into moles of electrons using the Faraday constant: moles e- = 48,300 / 96,500 = 0.5 mol. Since Ag+ + e- -> Ag is a 1:1 ratio, that's also 0.5 mol of silver. Multiply by silver's molar mass: 0.5 x 108 = 54.0g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following acts as both a reducing and an oxidizing agent?
questions.explanation: Look at where the key atom sits on its oxidation-state 'ladder'. In SO2, sulphur is at +4 - right in the middle of the range sulphur can adopt (from -2 up to +6). That gives it room to move both ways: it can be oxidized further (up to +6, as in H2SO4) or reduced (down toward 0 or lower), which is exactly why it can act as either a reducing or an oxidizing agent depending on what it reacts with.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following shows little or no net reaction when the volume of the system is decreased?
questions.explanation: Before worrying about direction, just count the moles of gas on each side of each equation. Pressure changes only shift an equilibrium when the two sides have different numbers of gas moles. For H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI, there are 2 moles of gas on both sides - so squeezing the volume doesn't favour either direction, and you barely see a shift.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: ZnO + CO → Zn + CO2. In the reaction above, zinc has been
questions.explanation: Track zinc's oxidation number through the reaction rather than just looking at the equation shape. In ZnO, zinc is +2. In elemental Zn, it's 0. That drop in oxidation number means zinc gained electrons - and gaining electrons is the definition of reduction. (CO, meanwhile, is oxidized to CO2, acting as the reducing agent that supplies those electrons.)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What volume of gas is evolved at s.t.p. if 2g of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) is added to a solution of hydrochloric acid? [Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, H = 1, molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm3]
questions.explanation: Start from the balanced equation: CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2. Molar mass of CaCO3 = 40 + 12 + (16x3) = 100 g/mol, so 2g is 0.02 mol. The CaCO3-to-CO2 ratio is 1:1, so you also get 0.02 mol of CO2. At s.t.p., 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 dm3 = 22,400 cm3, so the volume of CO2 = 0.02 x 22,400 = 448 cm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A chemical reaction is always associated with
options: a change in the nature of the reactants
a change in the volume of the reactants
an increase in the composition of one of the substances
questions.explanation: Strip this back to the core definition: what separates a chemical reaction from a physical change is that the atoms rearrange into genuinely new substances with different properties - not just a different shape, state, or volume of the same substance. That's the one thing that's always true, every single time.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When a solid substance disappears completely as a gas on heating, the substance is said to have undergone
questions.explanation: The giveaway phrase is 'disappears completely as a gas' - going straight from solid to gas, skipping the liquid stage entirely. That direct solid-to-gas jump is the definition of sublimation, seen with substances like iodine or ammonium chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If a solution contains 4.9g of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, calculate the amount of copper(II) oxide that will react with it. [Cu = 64, O = 16, S = 32, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Start with the balanced equation: CuO + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + H2O, a clean 1:1 mole ratio. Molar mass of H2SO4 = 2 + 32 + 64 = 98 g/mol, so 4.9g is 4.9 / 98 = 0.05 mol. Since the ratio is 1:1, you also need 0.05 mol of CuO. Molar mass of CuO = 64 + 16 = 80 g/mol, so mass = 0.05 x 80 = 4.0g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Vulcanization involves the removal of
questions.explanation: Picture what's happening at the molecular level: natural rubber (polyisoprene) is full of C=C double bonds along its chain. During vulcanization, sulphur atoms form cross-links right at those double bond sites, converting them into single bonds bridged by sulphur. That cross-linking is what makes vulcanized rubber stronger and more elastic - and it works by consuming the double bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: C2H5OH(aq) --[Conc. H2SO4 / 180°C]--> Y. In the reaction above, Y represents
questions.explanation: This is where the temperature detail matters more than students often expect: concentrated H2SO4 with ethanol behaves differently depending on how hot you go. At the higher temperature (around 180°C), the reaction favours elimination (dehydration) of a water molecule, producing the alkene ethene, C2H4. (Lower down, around 140°C with excess alcohol, the same reagents instead favour forming an ether.)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the production of soap, concentrated sodium chloride is added to
options: decrease the solubility of the soap
increase the solubility of the soap
questions.explanation: This step is called 'salting out'. Once the soap has already formed, adding concentrated NaCl sharply reduces how much of it can stay dissolved, so it precipitates out as a solid curd that floats free of the glycerol-and-water mixture, ready to be skimmed off and separated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Oxyacetylene flame is used for iron-welding because it
options: evolves a lot of heat when burnt
dissociates to produce carbon(IV) oxide and oxygen
makes the iron metal solidify very quickly
combines with oxygen to give a pop sound
questions.explanation: Welding needs enough energy to actually melt metal, and that's exactly what oxyacetylene delivers - burning acetylene in pure oxygen is intensely exothermic, reaching flame temperatures around 3000°C, hot enough to melt and fuse iron at the joint.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of these reagents can confirm the presence of a triple bond?
questions.explanation: The word 'confirm' is doing the heavy lifting here - you need a test that's specific to a triple bond, not one that also lights up for a double bond. Bromine (gas or water) and acidified KMnO4 both react with any C=C double bond too, so a positive result there doesn't tell you which kind of unsaturation you have. Ammoniacal copper(I) chloride is different: it reacts specifically with terminal alkynes, forming a distinctive red precipitate of copper acetylide - a positive result here really does confirm a triple bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Given the structure:
H   CH3
|   |
H3C - C - C - CH2 - CH2 - CH3
      |   |
     CH3  H
The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound above is
questions.explanation: Trace the longest continuous chain first before worrying about the branches. Counting along the main row gives six carbons - a hexane backbone. Now look at what's attached above and below the second and third carbons: each one carries a lone CH3 branch (plus its expected H). Numbering from the end that gives the lowest set of locants puts those two methyl branches at positions 2 and 3, giving 2,3-dimethylhexane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An isomer of C5H12 is
questions.explanation: Isomers of C5H12 must share that exact molecular formula while having a different structure. Checking each option's real formula settles it fast: butane and 2-methylpropane are both C4H10 - one carbon short, so neither can match C5H12 at all. '2-ethylbutane' isn't even a genuine distinct compound name (extending butane with an ethyl branch on carbon 2 just gives back a longer chain, correctly renamed 3-methylpentane). That leaves 2-methylbutane, which genuinely has the formula C5H12 and is one of pentane's real structural isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Alkanol + Alkanoic acid ⇌ Ester + Water. The reverse reaction of the equation above is known as
questions.explanation: Reversing the equation means breaking an ester back apart into its alcohol and acid using water - and 'breaking apart with water' is exactly what hydrolysis means, in the most general sense.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: CH3COOH(g) → CH4(g) + CO2(g). The reaction above is
questions.explanation: Look at exactly what's leaving the molecule: the carboxylic acid loses its -COOH group entirely as CO2, leaving just CH4 behind. Removing a carboxyl group as carbon dioxide is precisely the definition of decarboxylation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A characteristic of the alkane family is
questions.explanation: Alkanes are fully saturated - every carbon already has the maximum number of single bonds it can hold, so there's no double or triple bond available to react across. Instead, alkanes react by having one of their hydrogens swapped out for another atom, like in free-radical halogenation - a substitution reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Pollution of underground water by metal ions is very likely in a soil that has high
questions.explanation: Metal ions can only leach into groundwater once they're released as free, dissolved ions rather than locked up in insoluble soil minerals. Acidic soil (high H+ concentration) actively dissolves metal-bearing minerals and displaces metal ions from soil particles, freeing them up to migrate downward into the water table.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The solubility in mol dm-3 of 20g of CuSO4 dissolved in 100g of water at 18°C is [Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Work through this in two stages. First, find the moles dissolved: CuSO4's molar mass = 64 + 32 + (16x4) = 160 g/mol, so 20g is 20 / 160 = 0.125 mol - and that's per 100g (roughly 100 cm3) of water. To express solubility per dm3 (1000 cm3), scale that figure up by 10: 0.125 x 10 = 1.25 mol dm-3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of these compounds is a normal salt?
questions.explanation: A normal salt forms when ALL the replaceable (acidic) hydrogens of the parent acid have been swapped out for a metal ion, leaving none behind. Na2CO3 comes from carbonic acid with both of its acidic hydrogens replaced by sodium. Look closely at the other three options - each one still has a lone 'H' sitting in the formula, meaning one acidic hydrogen wasn't replaced, which makes them acid salts instead.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A carcinogenic substance is
questions.explanation: This is a straight recall point worth locking in: asbestos fibers are a well-documented carcinogen, and prolonged inhalation is linked to lung diseases including mesothelioma and lung cancer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What volume of 0.5 mol dm-3 H2SO4 will exactly neutralize 20 cm3 of 0.1 mol dm-3 NaOH solution?
questions.explanation: Start with the balanced equation: H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2H2O - notice 1 mole of acid neutralizes 2 moles of base, not a 1:1 match. Moles of NaOH = 0.020 dm3 x 0.1 mol dm-3 = 0.002 mol. Moles of H2SO4 needed = 0.002 / 2 = 0.001 mol. Volume of H2SO4 = moles / concentration = 0.001 / 0.5 = 0.002 dm3 = 2.0 cm3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Calcium tetraoxosulphate(VI) dissolves in water only sparingly to form a
questions.explanation: 'Sparingly soluble' just means a small, limited amount dissolves - it doesn't mean nothing dissolves at all. Whatever CaSO4 does go into solution is genuinely dissolved at the ion level, forming a true solution (just a dilute or weak one), not some in-between state like a colloid or suspension.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hardness of water is caused by the presence of the ions of
questions.explanation: This is testing whether you know what actually causes water hardness. Hard water contains dissolved calcium (Ca2+) and magnesium (Mg2+) ions, usually picked up as water passes through limestone or chalk deposits. These ions react with soap to form an insoluble scum instead of lather, and they're the ones responsible for the 'furring' you see in kettles. Sodium and potassium salts, by contrast, are almost always soluble and don't cause this problem - that's your quick test for eliminating options B and D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: It is difficult to achieve an orderly arrangement of the molecules of a gas because they
options: can collide with one another in the container
have little force of attraction between them
questions.explanation: Think about what makes solids orderly in the first place - strong intermolecular forces lock particles into fixed positions. Gas molecules have almost negligible forces of attraction between them, so nothing holds them in place; they fly around randomly and can't settle into a pattern. That weak attraction is the root cause - everything else you observe about gases (no fixed shape, constant collisions) flows from it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The shape of the s-orbital is
questions.explanation: This is straight recall from atomic structure: the s-orbital is spherical, meaning the probability of finding the electron is the same in every direction from the nucleus. That's what makes it different from p-orbitals, which are dumbbell-shaped and directional.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following mixtures of gases is likely to burn in flame?
questions.explanation: Scan each pair for a gas that's actually combustible. Helium and neon are both noble gases - completely unreactive, they won't burn under any normal condition. Nitrogen doesn't support or undergo combustion easily either. Hydrogen is the odd one out here: it's highly flammable and burns readily in air. Since hydrogen appears only in option C, that pairing is the one that will burn - neon just tags along inertly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The property of chlorine which causes hydrogen chloride to be more ionic than the chlorine molecule is its
questions.explanation: In Cl2, both atoms pull electrons equally hard, so the bond is purely covalent with no charge separation. In HCl, chlorine is far more electronegative than hydrogen, so it pulls the shared electron pair closer to itself, creating a partial negative charge on Cl and partial positive on H. That unequal pull - electronegativity - is exactly what gives HCl its extra ionic character compared to Cl2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the experiment above, X is a mixture of nitrogen, carbon(IV) oxide and
questions.explanation: This question comes from the classic 'rusting nail in trapped air' set-up, where a tube of air is inverted over water with an iron nail inside. As the iron rusts, it consumes the oxygen from the trapped air, and water rises to take up the volume oxygen used to occupy. What's left in the tube (X) is no longer oxygen - it's been used up - so X is really nitrogen (the bulk of air), a small residual amount of carbon(IV) oxide, and the inert/noble gases (like argon) that don't react with the rusting iron at all.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: A given volume of methane diffuses in 20s. How long will it take the same volume of sulphur(IV) oxide to diffuse under the same conditions? [C=12, H=1, S=32, O=16]
questions.explanation: This is Graham's Law: heavier gases diffuse more slowly, so they take longer. First, work out the molar masses - methane (CH4) = 12 + (4x1) = 16, and sulphur(IV) oxide (SO2) = 32 + (2x16) = 64. Graham's Law says time is proportional to the square root of molar mass, so t(SO2)/t(CH4) = sqrt(64/16) = sqrt(4) = 2. Since methane took 20s, SO2 - being 4 times heavier - takes twice as long: 20 x 2 = 40s.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine consists of two isotopes of mass numbers 35 and 37 in the ratio 3:1, and has an average atomic mass of 35.5. Calculate the relative abundance of the isotope of mass number 37.
questions.explanation: Don't rush past the ratio - 3:1 means out of every 4 parts, 3 are the lighter isotope (mass 35) and 1 is the heavier one (mass 37). Converting to percentages: Cl-35 makes up 3/4 = 75%, and Cl-37 makes up 1/4 = 25%. You can check this works: (0.75 x 35) + (0.25 x 37) = 26.25 + 9.25 = 35.5, which matches the given atomic mass exactly. The question asks specifically for the abundance of the mass-37 isotope, so the answer is 25%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An electron can be added to a halogen atom to form a halide ion with
questions.explanation: Halogens sit in Group 17, so a neutral halogen atom already has 7 valence electrons. The question specifically says an electron is added - that's what forms the halide ion (like Cl-). Adding one more electron to 7 gives 8, a full and stable octet. That's the whole reason halogens are so eager to gain an electron in the first place - it completes their outer shell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the nuclear equation Ra-226 (atomic number 88) decays to Rn-x (atomic number 86) by emitting an alpha particle, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: In any nuclear equation, mass number and atomic number must balance on both sides. An alpha particle is a helium nucleus (mass number 4, atomic number 2), so when radium emits one, it loses 4 from its mass number and 2 from its atomic number. Starting from radium's mass number of 226: 226 - 4 = 222. Check the atomic number too: 88 - 2 = 86, which matches radon's atomic number given in the equation - so x = 222 is confirmed from both sides balancing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: According to Charles's law, the volume of a gas becomes zero at
questions.explanation: Charles's law tells us that at constant pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature in Kelvin. If you extrapolate that straight-line relationship back to where volume would theoretically hit zero, you land on absolute zero - which is -273°C (0 K). Real gases actually liquefy before reaching this point, but the theoretical value the law points to is -273°C, and that's exactly why this temperature is called 'absolute zero'.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When steam is passed over red-hot carbon, the substances produced are
questions.explanation: This is the classic 'water gas' reaction: C(s) + H2O(g) → CO(g) + H2(g). Red-hot carbon isn't burning in excess oxygen here - it's reducing steam, pulling one oxygen atom off each water molecule to form carbon monoxide (carbon(II) oxide), while releasing hydrogen gas. The 'red-hot, limited-oxygen' setup is your cue that this is a reduction reaction producing CO, not full combustion producing CO2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aluminium hydroxide is used in the dyeing industry as a
questions.explanation: Aluminium hydroxide itself is colourless - it doesn't dye anything on its own. Its job is to act as a mordant: it forms a bridge between the fabric fibres and the dye molecule, fixing the colour in place so it doesn't wash out. Whenever you see a compound described as helping a dye 'stick' rather than providing colour itself, think mordant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Transition metals possess variable oxidation states because they have
options: a variable number of electrons in the p orbitals
questions.explanation: The defining feature of transition metals is their partially filled d orbitals, which sit very close in energy to the outer s orbital. Because the energy gap is so small, different numbers of d electrons can be lost or involved in bonding depending on the reaction, which is exactly why elements like iron or manganese show several different oxidation states instead of just one.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The allotrope of carbon used in the decolourization of sugar is
questions.explanation: Charcoal (specifically activated charcoal) has a huge internal surface area full of tiny pores, which lets it adsorb coloured impurity molecules out of a sugar solution as it passes through. None of the other carbon forms have this porous, adsorbing structure - that's the specific property this question is testing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Carbon is tetravalent because
options: all the atomic orbitals of carbon hybridize
the electrons in all the orbitals of carbon are equivalent
the electrons in both the 2s and 2p orbitals are equivalent
questions.explanation: Carbon's ground state is 1s2 2s2 2p2, which on its own would only give it two unpaired electrons. To form four bonds, one 2s electron is promoted into the empty 2p orbital, and then the 2s and three 2p orbitals mix together - hybridize - to form four identical sp3 orbitals. That hybridization step is exactly why carbon ends up tetravalent with four equivalent bonds, not just 'having' four electrons somewhere.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Sodium metal is always kept under oil because it
options: reacts with oxygen and carbon(IV) oxide
reacts vigorously on exposure to air
questions.explanation: Sodium is so reactive that ordinary air - its oxygen and moisture - will attack it almost immediately, tarnishing the shiny surface and eating into the metal. Oil is chosen as the storage medium precisely because it's unreactive and forms a barrier that excludes air completely. Don't rush to 'sodium reacts with water' here - that fact is actually why you'd never store it under water; oil is the safe, inert alternative that simply keeps air away.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Alloys are best prepared by
options: cooling a molten mixture of the metals
reducing a mixture of their metallic oxides
questions.explanation: An alloy is a homogeneous blend of metals at the atomic level, and the simplest way to achieve that is to melt the metals together so they mix thoroughly as liquids, then let the mixture cool and solidify into a uniform solid. That melt-and-cool process is what actually creates the intermingled structure that defines an alloy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Sulphur(IV) oxide bleaches by
questions.explanation: This is a favourite JAMB contrast question: chlorine bleaches by oxidation, but sulphur(IV) oxide bleaches by the opposite mechanism - reduction. SO2 donates electrons to the coloured compound, chemically altering it into a colourless form. Whenever you see 'SO2 bleaching', pair it with 'reduction' in your head, and pair 'chlorine bleaching' with 'oxidation' - that contrast is exactly what examiners like to test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following gases can be collected by the method of downward delivery?
questions.explanation: Downward delivery means the gas is piped down into an upright jar and, because it's denser than air, sinks to the bottom and pushes the lighter air out over the top. Chlorine (molar mass 71) is much denser than air (average molar mass about 29), so it fits this method perfectly. The trick to these questions is always to compare the gas's molar mass with air's - denser gases go by downward delivery, lighter ones need the inverted-jar 'upward delivery' method instead.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When calcium oxide is heated with carbon, the oxide will
options: be converted to the trioxocarbonate(IV) salt
questions.explanation: This is the industrial reaction for making calcium carbide: CaO + 3C → CaC2 + CO, carried out at very high temperature in an electric furnace. Carbon doesn't just reduce CaO to the free metal here - calcium is too reactive for carbon to pull it all the way to the elemental state under these conditions. Instead, carbon combines directly with the calcium to form the carbide, releasing carbon monoxide as the by-product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A solution which, on treatment with hydrochloric acid, produces a colourless, odourless gas that turns limewater milky is most likely to be a
questions.explanation: 'Turns limewater milky' is the signature confirmatory test for carbon(IV) oxide gas - nothing else on this list produces that reaction. Carbonates (trioxocarbonate(IV) salts) react with HCl to release CO2: CO3^2- + 2H+ → H2O + CO2. Whenever you see 'milky limewater' in a question, your mind should jump straight to CO2, and from there straight to a carbonate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The soft solder used for welding and plumbing is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Soft solder is a lead-tin alloy, valued precisely because mixing the two metals gives a much lower melting point than either metal alone - exactly what you need for joining pipes and wires without damaging them with excessive heat.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reddish-brown rust on iron roofing sheets consists of
questions.explanation: Rust isn't a single dry oxide - it forms when iron reacts with both oxygen and moisture in the air, so it comes out as hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3.xH2O, where x is a variable amount of water trapped in the structure. That water content is exactly why rust looks flaky and porous rather than like a solid metallic oxide coating.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Na2S2O3(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) + ... . Which of the following would introduce the greatest increase in the rate of the chemical reaction above?
options: An increase in temperature and a decrease in the concentration of the reactant
A decrease in the volume and an increase in the pressure of the reactant
A decrease in the temperature and an increase in the concentration of the reactant
An increase in temperature and an increase in the concentration of the reactant
questions.explanation: Rate of reaction responds to both temperature and concentration in the same direction - raising either one speeds things up, because you get more particles moving faster (more frequent, more energetic collisions) and more particles packed into the same space (more frequent collisions overall). To get the greatest possible increase, you want both factors pushing the rate up at once, which only happens in option D. Pressure and volume changes matter for gas-phase reactions, but this is an aqueous solution reaction, so they're irrelevant here.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The tincture of iodine means iodine dissolved in
questions.explanation: Tincture of iodine is the familiar antiseptic solution made by dissolving iodine in a mixture of ethanol and water (with a trace of potassium iodide to help it dissolve). Iodine is only very sparingly soluble in water on its own, which is exactly why the alcohol is needed to get it into solution in the first place.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cu2+(aq) + 4NH3(aq) ↔ [Cu(NH3)4]2+(aq). In the reaction above, what is the effect of precipitating Cu2+(aq) as CuS(s)?
options: More NH3 is released as the equilibrium shifts to the left
The equilibrium will shift to the right
questions.explanation: Cu2+ sits on the left side of this equilibrium, as one of the reactants forming the deep-blue complex ion. If you precipitate Cu2+ out of solution as insoluble CuS, you're constantly removing it from the left side. By Le Chatelier's principle, the system responds by shifting to replace what's being removed - that means the equilibrium shifts left, and the complex ion [Cu(NH3)4]2+ breaks back down to regenerate Cu2+ (which then gets precipitated again), releasing free NH3 into the solution as a result.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Copper and silver metals are commonly used as coins because they are
questions.explanation: A good coin metal needs to keep its shine and resist corrosion through years of handling. Copper and silver sit low in the reactivity series, meaning they don't readily lose electrons to oxygen or moisture in the air - in other words, they're not easily oxidized. That resistance to tarnishing and corroding is exactly why they've historically been chosen for coinage.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following sets of metals dissolves in dilute HCl?
questions.explanation: The rule here is simple: only metals positioned above hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace it from dilute acid and dissolve. Magnesium, tin, and iron all sit above hydrogen, so all three react with dilute HCl to release hydrogen gas and dissolve as chloride salts. Copper sits below hydrogen - it simply can't do this. The trick with this question is to check every single metal in each set, because one 'bad' metal (copper) is enough to disqualify the whole option.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If chlorine is bubbled into water and the resulting yellowish-green solution is exposed to bright sunlight for a while, the solution will decompose, giving out
options: oxygen and leaving behind aqueous hydrochloric acid
questions.explanation: Don't rush past what's already happened by the time you get to the 'sunlight' step. When chlorine first dissolves in water, it reacts to form a mixture of hydrochloric acid and hypochlorous acid: Cl2 + H2O ↔ HCl + HOCl. It's this hypochlorous acid that's unstable in sunlight and breaks down further: 2HOCl → 2HCl + O2. So the gas given off is oxygen, and what's left behind in solution is aqueous hydrochloric acid - the hypochlorous acid has already been consumed in the process, not produced by it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: H3PO4(aq) + H2O(l) ↔ H2PO4-(aq) + H3O+(aq), ΔH = -13kJ at 298K. In the reaction above, an increase in temperature would
options: have no effect on the reaction
questions.explanation: The negative ΔH tells you the forward reaction releases heat - it's exothermic. That automatically makes the reverse reaction endothermic (it absorbs heat). By Le Chatelier's principle, adding heat to a system pushes the equilibrium in whichever direction soaks up that extra heat, so raising the temperature here favours the reverse (endothermic) reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction that takes place in Daniell's cell is
questions.explanation: In a Daniell cell, zinc metal loses electrons (oxidation) at one electrode while copper ions gain electrons (reduction) at the other, with the electrons travelling through an external wire to generate current. That paired loss-and-gain of electrons is the definition of a redox reaction, and it's exactly what makes the whole cell work as a source of electricity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What happens when a zinc rod is immersed in copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution?
options: The blue colour of the solution disappears
Electrons flow from copper to zinc
The copper generates more copper ions
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper straight out of solution: Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) → Zn2+(aq) + Cu(s). As the reaction proceeds, blue Cu2+ ions are steadily replaced by colourless Zn2+ ions, so the characteristic blue colour of the copper sulphate solution gradually fades away, while a coating of reddish-brown copper metal builds up on the zinc rod.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: C2H4(g) + H2(g) → C2H6(g), ΔH = -137 kJ mol-1. The reaction represented above is
questions.explanation: The sign of ΔH tells you everything you need here: a negative value means the reaction releases heat into the surroundings as it happens, which is precisely the definition of exothermic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The salt formed from a strong acid and a strong base is
questions.explanation: When a strong acid and a strong base react, both the resulting cation and anion are 'spectator' ions that don't hydrolyse in water - neither one pulls the solution's pH away from 7. Think of table salt, NaCl, formed from HCl and NaOH: it dissolves to give a perfectly neutral solution. That's the general rule for strong-acid-plus-strong-base salts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Dissolving some pellets of NaOH in water would result in
options: a decrease in the free energy of the solution
a decrease in the entropy of the solution
a lowering of the temperature of the solution
an increase in the entropy of the solution
questions.explanation: Picture what's physically happening: solid NaOH starts out as a rigid, highly ordered ionic lattice, with every Na+ and OH- locked into a fixed position. Once it dissolves, those ions break free and disperse randomly throughout the water. That's a clear jump from an ordered state to a disordered one, which is exactly what an increase in entropy means. This is also a good demonstration reaction because it's noticeably exothermic - the container gets warm, not cold - so you can rule out any option that claims cooling.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A metal X forms two bromides with the formulae XBr2 and XBr3. What type of bonding exists between X and bromine in the bromides?
questions.explanation: The clue here is the variable charge - X shows up as both 2+ and 3+, which is exactly the kind of behaviour you see in a metal that loses different numbers of electrons depending on the reaction. That electron loss is the signature of ionic bonding: X transfers electrons to the highly electronegative bromine atoms, forming X2+ or X3+ cations alongside Br- anions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A mixture of petrol and water can be separated through
options: the use of a separating funnel
questions.explanation: Petrol and water don't mix - they're immiscible liquids that naturally settle into two distinct layers based on density, with petrol floating on top of water. That's exactly the situation a separating funnel is designed for: you simply let the layers settle and run off the bottom layer through the tap, leaving the top layer behind.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: CH3CH2Cl + KCN → CH3CH2CN + KCl. In the reaction above, the cyanide is
questions.explanation: Look at what's actually happening in this reaction: the cyanide ion (CN-) is electron-rich, and it attacks the carbon atom that's bonded to the electronegative, electron-poor chlorine. That's a species donating a pair of electrons to form a new bond - the defining behaviour of a nucleophile ('nucleus-loving'). This is a classic SN2 substitution, and cyanide's role as the attacking nucleophile is exactly what makes it work.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The hydrocarbon used in the production of styrene is
questions.explanation: Styrene production starts by reacting benzene with ethene in a Friedel-Crafts alkylation to form ethylbenzene, which is then dehydrogenated to give styrene. Ethene's reactive carbon-carbon double bond is exactly what makes it suitable for that alkylation step - the saturated, unreactive ethane can't do this job.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many structural isomers of chlorobutane are possible?
questions.explanation: Don't just think about moving the chlorine along one carbon chain - remember butane itself has two skeletal forms: straight-chain and branched. On the straight chain, chlorine can sit on carbon 1 or carbon 2 (giving 1-chlorobutane and 2-chlorobutane). On the branched skeleton (2-methylpropane), chlorine can sit on a terminal carbon or on the central carbon (giving 1-chloro-2-methylpropane and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane). That's four genuinely distinct structures in total.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The conversion of open chain alkanes into cycloalkanes and aromatic compounds is called
questions.explanation: Reforming is the specific petroleum-refining process that reshapes straight-chain alkane molecules into rings - cycloalkanes and aromatic compounds - using heat and a catalyst. It's done industrially to boost the octane rating of petrol, since ring-shaped and aromatic molecules burn more smoothly in engines than their straight-chain counterparts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following alkanes has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Among alkanes, boiling point climbs steadily as the carbon chain gets longer. Longer chains have more surface area in contact with neighbouring molecules, which means stronger van der Waals forces holding the molecules together - and stronger intermolecular forces mean you need more energy (a higher temperature) to boil the liquid. Of the four given, pentane (C5H12) has the longest chain, so it has the highest boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Certain useful waxes are composed mainly of
questions.explanation: Waxes are esters - formed when a long-chain alkanoic acid reacts with a long-chain alkanol (a single monohydric alcohol, unlike the glycerol used in fats). The resulting ester compound is named as an 'alkanoate', and that ester itself is what makes up the wax, not the free alcohol or acid on its own.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When temporary hard water is boiled for some time in a kettle, the inner surface of the kettle becomes coated with a deposit of
questions.explanation: Temporary hardness comes from dissolved calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV), Ca(HCO3)2, which is soluble and stays invisible in the water. Boiling drives off the dissolved CO2 and water, and the reaction Ca(HCO3)2 → CaCO3 + H2O + CO2 converts that soluble compound into insoluble calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) - which is exactly the chalky 'fur' or limescale you see building up inside a kettle over time.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A supersaturated solution is said to contain
options: more solute than it can dissolve at that temperature in the presence of undissolved solute
as much solute as it can dissolve at that temperature in the presence of undissolved solute
as much solute as it can dissolve at that temperature
more solute than it can dissolve at that temperature
questions.explanation: The key idea with supersaturation is that ALL of the excess solute is still dissolved - there's no visible undissolved solid sitting at the bottom. It's an unstable, 'overloaded' state where the solution holds more solute than it normally could at that temperature, often achieved by dissolving solute at a higher temperature and then carefully cooling without disturbance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
questions.question: The presence of nitrogen in air is to slow down
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air and is largely chemically inert - its main practical role is to dilute the oxygen. If air were pure oxygen instead of a nitrogen-oxygen mix, both combustion and respiration would happen far too violently and rapidly to be safe or sustainable. Nitrogen's dilution effect moderates the pace of these two everyday oxygen-driven processes to something manageable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A good drying agent should be
questions.explanation: A drying agent's whole job is to pull moisture out of its surroundings - that general affinity for absorbing water vapour from the air or a gas stream is exactly what 'hygroscopic' means, and it's the property examiners are testing for here. Deliquescence is a more extreme, related idea (absorbing so much water the solid dissolves into a puddle), but 'hygroscopic' is the standard umbrella term used to describe the desired property of a desiccant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Smog usually occurs over cities which
options: burn a lot of fossil fuels
questions.explanation: Smog - a blend of 'smoke' and 'fog' - forms when pollutants from burning fossil fuels (vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions) build up in the air and react with atmospheric moisture and sunlight. The direct root cause the question is testing is that fossil fuel combustion, not any secondary factor about the city's geography or population alone.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A student records the length of a table as 120.0 cm using a metre rule. The percentage error in this measurement is
questions.explanation: Correct: The smallest division of a metre rule is 1 mm = 0.1 cm. Percentage error = (0.1/120.0) × 100 = 0.083%. B is wrong as it corresponds to an error of about 1 mm in 12 cm, not 120 cm. C is wrong as it corresponds to an error of roughly 10 cm, far too large. D is wrong as it's unrealistically small for a metre rule's precision.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following graphs correctly represents uniform acceleration?
options: A straight line velocity-time graph with positive slope
questions.explanation: Correct: Uniform acceleration means velocity changes at a constant rate; on a v-t graph, this gives a straight line with positive slope (since slope of a v-t graph = acceleration). A is wrong because a curved d-t graph shows changing velocity, but not necessarily uniform acceleration. B is wrong because a horizontal v-t graph means zero acceleration (constant velocity). D is wrong because a straight d-t graph means constant velocity, hence zero acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object moves in a circle of radius 2 m with angular velocity 3 rad s⁻¹. The centripetal acceleration is
questions.explanation: Correct: Centripetal acceleration a = ω²r = (3)² × 2 = 9 × 2 = 18 ms⁻². B is wrong because 6 = ωr equals the linear velocity, not acceleration. C is wrong because 9 = ω² alone, forgetting to multiply by r. D is wrong because 1.5 = r/ω² is an incorrect formula.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A satellite is in a parking (geostationary) orbit. Which of the following is TRUE of this satellite?
options: It orbits at any altitude with any period
Its period equals 24 hours and it remains above the same point on Earth
It moves faster than Earth's rotation
It must orbit over the poles
questions.explanation: Correct: A geostationary satellite orbits at roughly 36,000 km above the equator with a period of 24 hours, matching Earth's rotation, so it appears stationary to an observer on the ground. A is wrong because a parking orbit has one specific altitude (~36,000 km) and period (24 hrs), not any combination. C is wrong because its orbital period matches Earth's rotation exactly — it's the same rotational speed, not faster. D is wrong because geostationary satellites orbit over the equator, not the poles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Lami's theorem applies when
options: Three non-parallel concurrent forces are in equilibrium
Two forces act in the same direction
Forces act on a rigid body at different points
questions.explanation: Correct: Lami's theorem states that if three concurrent coplanar forces are in equilibrium, each force is proportional to the sine of the angle between the other two; it requires exactly three non-parallel concurrent forces in equilibrium. A is wrong because parallel forces don't meet at a single point, and Lami's theorem requires concurrent forces. C is wrong because two forces in the same direction cannot balance a third unless they sum to zero, which isn't the general case. D is wrong because forces acting at different points require the principle of moments, not Lami's theorem.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform beam of weight 200 N and length 4 m is supported at its ends. A load of 300 N is placed 1 m from one end. The reaction at the end closest to the load is
questions.explanation: Correct: Taking moments about the far end: R₁ × 4 = 300 × 3 + 200 × 2 = 900 + 400 = 1300, so R₁ = 1300/4 = 325 N. Note: the document's stated correct answer is B (225 N) though its own worked explanation arrives at 325 N — this appears to be an inconsistency in the source material worth double-checking. A is described as a calculation error in the moment arm. C is described as ignoring the beam's own weight. D is described as taking moments about the wrong end.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A force of 10 N acts on a body and moves it 5 m in the direction of the force. The work done by the force is
questions.explanation: Correct: Work = Force × displacement × cos θ; since force and displacement are in the same direction, θ = 0°, cos 0° = 1, so W = 10 × 5 × 1 = 50 J. B is wrong because 2 J = F/d divides instead of multiplying. C is wrong because 15 J = F + d adds instead of multiplying. D is wrong because 0 J would apply only when force is perpendicular to displacement (cos 90° = 0).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The coefficient of limiting friction between two surfaces is 0.4. If the normal reaction is 50 N, the limiting frictional force is
questions.explanation: Correct: F = μN = 0.4 × 50 = 20 N, the maximum static friction before the object begins to slide. B is wrong because 125 N = N/μ inverts the correct relationship. C is wrong because 0.008 N = μ/N uses the wrong operation. D is wrong because 50.4 N = N + μ incorrectly adds the two values instead of multiplying.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The velocity ratio of a pulley system with 4 pulleys arranged in a block and tackle system is
questions.explanation: Correct: In a block and tackle system, the velocity ratio equals the number of rope segments supporting the load, which equals the number of pulleys, so with 4 pulleys, VR = 4. B is wrong because 2 is the VR for a single movable pulley setup instead. C is wrong because 8 would require 8 supporting rope sections. D is wrong because 16 has no basis given 4 pulleys in this arrangement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A simple mercury barometer reads 760 mm Hg. The atmospheric pressure in Pascals is (density of mercury = 13,600 kgm⁻³, g = 10 ms⁻²)
questions.explanation: Correct: P = ρgh = 13600 × 10 × 0.76 = 103,360 Pa ≈ 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa, close to standard atmospheric pressure of approximately 101,325 Pa. B is wrong because it results from an incorrect depth or calculation error. C is wrong because 7.6 × 10⁴ omits the density of mercury from the calculation. D is wrong because 0.76 × 10³ = 760 Pa simply converts mm to m without applying ρg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: As altitude increases, atmospheric pressure
options: Increases because the atmosphere is denser
Decreases because there is less air above
questions.explanation: Correct: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the air above a point; as altitude increases, there is less air above, so the pressure decreases, which is why mountain climbers need supplemental oxygen. A is wrong because the atmosphere actually becomes LESS dense at higher altitude, so pressure decreases. B is wrong because pressure clearly varies with altitude — it doesn't stay constant. D is wrong because pressure decreases monotonically with altitude within the troposphere, not in an increase-then-decrease pattern.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body of mass 100 g weighs 0.8 N when immersed in a liquid. Its weight in air is 1.0 N (g = 10 ms⁻²). The relative density of the liquid is
questions.explanation: Correct: Upthrust = Weight in air − Weight in liquid = 1.0 − 0.8 = 0.2 N. Working through the volume and density relationships as shown in the source explanation (with body density = 10,000 kg/m³ and equal-volume water weight = 0.1 N), the relative density = 0.2/0.1 = 2. A is wrong because 4 incorrectly divides weight in air by upthrust in the wrong combination. B is wrong because 0.25 inverts the correct ratio. D is wrong because 0.5 uses an incorrect ratio arrangement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The Newton's law of cooling method is used to determine
options: Specific heat capacity of liquids by plotting temperature against time
questions.explanation: Correct: Newton's law of cooling states that the rate of heat loss is proportional to the temperature difference between a body and its surroundings; the resulting cooling curve (temperature vs time) is used to determine specific heat capacity by comparing the cooling rates of a test liquid against a reference liquid. A is wrong because linear expansivity is measured using expansion instruments, not cooling curves. C is wrong because latent heat is measured by the method of mixtures or electrical heating, not cooling curves. D is wrong because Newton's law applies broadly to the cooling process, not just to finding a boiling point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Structure of matter and kinetic theory
questions.question: According to the kinetic theory of gases, the pressure exerted by a gas is due to
options: The weight of gas molecules pressing down
Collisions of gas molecules with the walls of the container
The repulsive forces between gas molecules
The temperature of the gas only
questions.explanation: Correct: Gas pressure results from the rate of momentum transfer as molecules bombard the container walls; P = ⅓ρ<c²>, where more collisions and greater momentum per collision produce higher pressure. A is wrong because gas pressure acts in all directions, not just downward — weight is not the cause. C is wrong because in an ideal gas, intermolecular forces are neglected — repulsion between molecules is not considered. D is wrong because while temperature affects molecular speed and hence pressure, pressure itself has a direct mechanical cause (collisions), not temperature alone.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a transverse wave?
options: Particles vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation
Particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
The wave can travel through a vacuum only
questions.explanation: Correct: In transverse waves, particle oscillation is perpendicular to the wave's travel direction, as seen in light waves, water ripples, and waves on a string. A is wrong because vibration parallel to propagation describes LONGITUDINAL waves, like sound. C is wrong because although light (a transverse wave) can travel through vacuum, not all transverse waves require it — string waves, for instance, need a medium. D is wrong because transverse and longitudinal are opposite, mutually exclusive wave types.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The phenomenon of diffraction is best observed when
options: The wavelength is much smaller than the obstacle or opening
The wavelength is approximately equal to or larger than the obstacle or opening
The wave travels in a straight line
questions.explanation: Correct: Diffraction, the bending of waves around obstacles, is most pronounced when the wavelength is approximately equal to the size of the obstacle; when wavelength is much larger than the obstacle, waves pass with minimal diffraction, and when much smaller, they cast a clear geometric shadow. A is wrong because a small wavelength relative to the obstacle actually gives poor diffraction. C is wrong because straight-line travel indicates no diffraction is occurring. D is wrong because total reflection is a distinctly different wave behavior from diffraction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The principle of superposition of waves states that
options: Two waves always cancel each other
The resultant displacement at any point is the algebraic sum of individual displacements of waves at that point
Waves must be of the same frequency to superpose
Superposition only occurs with light waves
questions.explanation: Correct: The superposition principle states that when two or more waves overlap, the total displacement equals the algebraic (vector) sum of the individual displacements, leading to constructive or destructive interference. A is wrong because waves can either cancel (destructive) OR reinforce (constructive) — they don't always cancel. C is wrong because waves of different frequencies can also superpose, producing beats. D is wrong because superposition applies to all wave types, including sound and water waves, not just light.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The Doppler effect explains the change in observed frequency when
options: There is relative motion between the source and observer
The amplitude of the wave changes
Two waves interfere with each other
A wave is reflected from a surface
questions.explanation: Correct: The Doppler effect describes how, when a source moves toward an observer, waves are compressed (shorter wavelength, higher frequency), while moving away stretches the waves (longer wavelength, lower frequency); this is used in radar, astronomy (red shift), and medical ultrasound. B is wrong because amplitude change affects loudness or intensity, not frequency. C is wrong because interference involves the superposition of waves, not a frequency shift. D is wrong because reflection from a surface can cause an echo, but the frequency change is Doppler-related only if there is also relative motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Total internal reflection occurs when
options: Light travels from less dense to more dense medium
The angle of incidence is less than the critical angle
Light travels from a denser medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle
The refractive index is less than 1
questions.explanation: Correct: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser to a less dense medium AND the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, causing all light to be reflected back into the denser medium with none refracted. A is wrong because light must travel FROM a denser medium TO a less dense one — not the other way around. B is wrong because the angle must EXCEED the critical angle; below it, refraction still occurs normally. D is wrong because refractive index is greater than 1 for a denser medium — n < 1 doesn't produce total internal reflection.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A short-sighted (myopic) person cannot see distant objects clearly because
options: The image of distant objects forms behind the retina
The image of distant objects forms in front of the retina due to an over-curved lens or elongated eyeball
questions.explanation: Correct: Myopia occurs because the eye's lens is too curved or the eyeball too long, so parallel rays from distant objects converge BEFORE reaching the retina; it's corrected with a diverging (concave) lens. A is wrong because an image forming behind the retina describes hyperopia (long-sightedness), not myopia. C is wrong because pupil dilation affects the amount of light entering, not the focusing of the image. D is wrong because retinal sensitivity is unrelated to refractive errors like myopia.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A person can see objects clearly only between 25 cm and 150 cm. This person has
options: Both myopia (cannot see beyond 150 cm) and presbyopia
questions.explanation: Correct: Normal near point is 25 cm and far point is infinity; this person's far point is limited to 150 cm, indicating myopia (unable to focus beyond 150 cm), and the near-point limitation also suggests presbyopia (loss of accommodation). A is wrong because the additional near-point limitation suggests more than just simple myopia alone. B is wrong because hyperopia means difficulty seeing near objects, yet this person can see clearly at 25 cm. D is wrong because normal vision has a far point at infinity, not limited to 150 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Charging by induction produces a charge on the conductor that is
options: The same sign as the inducing charge
Opposite in sign to the inducing charge, without contact
Distributed only on the surface facing the inducing charge
questions.explanation: Correct: In charging by induction, a charged object is brought near a conductor; opposite charges accumulate near it while like charges move to the far end, and if the conductor is then earthed and the inducing charge removed, it retains a charge opposite to the inducing charge. A is wrong because a charge of the same sign as the inducing charge is instead produced by charging by CONTACT (conduction). C is wrong because the net charge is not zero on the induced conductor once the induction process is complete. D is wrong because after earthing during induction, the charge redistributes over the entire conductor, not just one facing surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three capacitors of capacitances 2 μF, 4 μF, and 6 μF are connected in parallel. The total capacitance is
questions.explanation: Correct: For capacitors in parallel, C_total = C₁ + C₂ + C₃ = 2 + 4 + 6 = 12 μF, since parallel capacitances simply add directly. B is wrong because 1.09 μF is instead the series combination value (1/C = 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/6 ≈ 1/1.09). C is wrong because 0.92 μF results from an error in a series-style calculation. D is wrong because 24 μF is the product of the values, which isn't relevant to a parallel combination.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. The effective resistance is
questions.explanation: Correct: 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1, so R = 1 Ω. A is wrong because 11 Ω = 2 + 3 + 6 mistakenly applies the series formula. C is wrong because 0.09 Ω results from an arithmetic error. D is wrong because 6 Ω uses only one of the resistor values instead of combining all three.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In Kirchhoff's current law, the sum of currents entering a junction equals
options: The sum of currents leaving the junction
questions.explanation: Correct: Kirchhoff's Current Law states that the algebraic sum of currents at any junction = 0, equivalently expressed as ΣI_in = ΣI_out, based on the conservation of charge. A is wrong because the sum is zero only when currents entering are algebraically combined with currents leaving as negative — option B states the relationship more directly. C is wrong because EMF is not related to the current balance at a junction. D is wrong because voltage at a junction is determined by Kirchhoff's Voltage Law, not the current law.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: Correct: Fleming's left-hand rule (the motor rule) uses the thumb for thrust/force, index finger for field (B), and middle finger for conventional current direction, and is used for motors and current-in-field force problems. A is wrong because Fleming's right-hand rule is instead the generator rule, used for determining induced EMF direction. C is wrong because the right-hand screw rule determines the direction of B around a straight current-carrying wire, a different application. D is wrong because the right-hand grip rule also determines the direction of B around a conductor, not the force on it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A galvanometer is converted to an ammeter by connecting
questions.explanation: Correct: Ammeter conversion involves connecting a shunt, a low resistance, in parallel with the galvanometer, so most of the current bypasses the galvanometer through the shunt, allowing measurement of larger currents while protecting the galvanometer. A is wrong because a high resistance in series instead converts a galvanometer to a VOLTMETER, not an ammeter. C is wrong because a capacitor in series would block DC, making it useless for DC ammeters. D is wrong because inductors are not used in the process of galvanometer conversion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Einstein's photoelectric equation is E = hf = φ + ½mv². Here φ represents
options: The kinetic energy of the emitted electron
The work function — minimum energy to release an electron from the metal surface
The total energy of the photon after emission
questions.explanation: Correct: In hf = φ + KE_max, hf is the photon energy, φ (the work function) is the energy used to overcome surface binding, and ½mv² is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electron. A is wrong because ½mv² is the kinetic energy term — φ specifically represents the work function, a separate quantity. C is wrong because frequency f appears within the term hf, while φ represents the work function, not frequency itself. D is wrong because after emission, the photon has already been absorbed — it has no leftover energy afterward.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Alpha particles are deflected more by electric and magnetic fields than beta particles because
options: Alpha particles have greater charge-to-mass ratio
Alpha particles are larger and slower with higher charge
Beta particles travel faster (approaching speed of light) with much less charge
Both A and C are correct
questions.explanation: Correct: Note this question's phrasing appears inverted relative to its own answer — beta particles are actually deflected MORE than alpha particles, since beta particles (electrons) move at near light speed with only −1e charge, while alpha particles have +2e charge but are far heavier (about 7300× the electron mass) and slower, so despite their higher charge, alphas are deflected LESS. A is wrong because alpha's charge-to-mass ratio (2e/4u) is actually LESS than that of beta particles (e/0.00055u). B is wrong because size doesn't determine deflection in a field — charge and momentum are what matter. D is wrong since option A is incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A transistor can be used as an amplifier because
options: A small base current controls a much larger collector current, producing a larger output signal
It has three terminals instead of two
It operates on both AC and DC
It is made of semiconductor material
questions.explanation: Correct: Transistor amplification works because a small input current at the base (I_B) controls a much larger collector current (I_C = hFE × I_B, where hFE is the current gain, typically 50–300), allowing a small input signal to produce a larger output signal. B is wrong because having three terminals is simply a physical fact about transistors, not the reason for amplification. C is wrong because operating on both AC and DC is a general characteristic, not the specific mechanism behind amplification. D is wrong because being a semiconductor is what makes transistors work in general, but it doesn't specifically explain the amplification mechanism.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: In comprehension passages, the MAIN purpose of identifying a 'topic sentence' is to _____.
options: determine the background of the writer
locate the central idea of a paragraph
identify the conclusion of the passage
find all supporting details in a passage
questions.explanation: A topic sentence states the central idea of a paragraph. It is usually the first or last sentence. JAMB often asks candidates to identify it because it carries the paragraph's controlling idea.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: When a writer makes a statement that is NOT explicitly stated but can be reasoned from available clues, the reader is expected to _____.
questions.explanation: An inference is a conclusion drawn from evidence and reasoning rather than from direct statement. JAMB regularly tests 'implied meaning' through inference questions.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: A 'cloze test' as used in JAMB is designed primarily to test a candidate's ability to _____.
options: identify figures of speech within texts
understand context and supply appropriate words
questions.explanation: In a cloze test, words are removed from a passage and the candidate must fill gaps using contextual understanding and grammar knowledge. It tests reading comprehension, vocabulary in context, and coherence.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: Read the sentence: 'Despite the torrential rain, the farmer ploughed on.' The underlined phrase 'ploughed on' is best interpreted as _____.
questions.explanation: 'Ploughed on' is an idiomatic expression meaning to continue doing something despite difficulties. The context of 'despite the torrential rain' confirms the idea of persistence.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes 'synthesis of ideas' as tested in JAMB comprehension?
options: The ability to memorise all the facts in a passage
The ability to translate a passage into another language
The act of combining separate pieces of information to form a complete whole
The ability to identify grammatical errors in a passage
questions.explanation: The JAMB syllabus explicitly defines synthesis as 'the art of combining distinct or separate pieces of information to form a complete whole as summary.' This is the exact definition JAMB tests.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: In a comprehension passage, 'coherence' refers to _____.
options: the logical flow and connection of ideas
the length and complexity of paragraphs
questions.explanation: Coherence in a passage means that ideas are logically connected and flow smoothly from one to another. JAMB tests 'coherence and logical reasoning' under comprehension objectives.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: A JAMB passage ends with the sentence: 'All these considered, the government must act now.' This sentence most likely serves as _____.
options: a topic sentence introducing a new idea
a concluding sentence that synthesises the argument
questions.explanation: The phrase 'All these considered' shows that the writer is wrapping up by drawing together the points already made. This is a summary-conclusion function, which JAMB links to synthesis and logical reasoning.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: In the sentence 'The director, along with his aides, was present at the function,' the mood conveyed is _____.
questions.explanation: The diction ('director', 'aides', 'function') signals a formal, official setting. JAMB tests 'writer's mood' and this sentence communicates an official/formal occasion.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: The writer of a passage states: 'One cannot but wonder at the audacity of these officials.' The writer's ATTITUDE toward the officials is _____.
questions.explanation: 'Audacity' used in this context implies brazenness or recklessness. The construction 'one cannot but wonder' expresses incredulous disapproval. JAMB tests attitude and tone regularly.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: Which description BEST defines an 'expository' type of passage?
options: A passage that tells a story with characters and events
A passage that presents and explains facts and information
A passage that tries to convince the reader to accept an opinion
A passage that paints a vivid picture of a scene
questions.explanation: Exposition presents factual information, explains concepts, or informs. JAMB tests four passage types: description, narration, exposition, and argumentation/persuasion.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: From the context: 'The old man was garrulous; he never stopped talking from morning till night.' The word 'garrulous' means _____.
questions.explanation: The context clause 'he never stopped talking from morning till night' directly defines 'garrulous.' JAMB always provides context clues in comprehension vocabulary questions.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an ARGUMENTATIVE passage?
options: A narrative about a village boy who became a professor
A description of the landmarks of Lagos city
An explanation of how photosynthesis works in plants
A text claiming that corporal punishment should be abolished in schools
questions.explanation: Argumentation/persuasion presents a stance on an issue and tries to convince the reader. Option D makes a claim and implies a call for action — the hallmark of argumentation.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: In The Lekki Headmaster, Mr. Bepo Adewale served as principal of which school?
questions.explanation: Mr. Bepo Adewale is the principal of Stardom Schools in Lekki, Lagos. This is the primary setting of the novel. He had previously been at Beesway and helped found Fruitful Future.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: In Chapter 1 ('Dusk'), Bepo's unusual behaviour at the school assembly was that he _____.
options: resigned publicly in front of students
broke down crying at the podium
questions.explanation: Chapter 1 opens with Bepo approaching the podium but breaking into tears instead of speaking. This shocking emotional breakdown sets the entire novel's tension in motion.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: The nickname 'The Lekki Headmaster' was given to Bepo because he _____.
options: lived in Lekki all his life
humorously imitated characters from the TV drama Village Headmaster
was the most feared headmaster in Lekki
questions.explanation: The nickname originated from Bepo's habit of mimicking characters from the old Nigerian TV show 'Village Headmaster' during his time at Stardom Kiddies. His colleagues adopted it affectionately.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: In Chapter 5 ('Snake in the Roof'), the phrase 'hanging a snake in the roof' was used by the MD's mother to describe _____.
options: the danger of keeping exotic pets in school
the cooperative society's wealth as a potential threat
the risk of hiring dishonest staff
the illegal activities of staff members
questions.explanation: Chief Mrs. Solape Bayo used this metaphor to caution that the school cooperative's accumulated ₦95 million and loans were like a 'snake in the roof' — dangerous wealth that could cause harm if mismanaged.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: In Chapter 6, the grammar controversy was about the sentence _____.
options: 'He and she comes to school everyday'
'The staff of the school are hardworking'
'Ade as well as Jide comes early'
'Neither the boys nor the girl were present'
questions.explanation: Mr. Guta, a parent, was furious about the sentence 'Ade as well as Jide comes early' written in his son's notebook by Mr. Fafore. Bepo defended the correctness of the singular verb 'comes' when 'as well as' is used.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: Bepo's CORRECT grammatical explanation in Chapter 6 was that with the connective 'as well as', the verb _____.
options: must be plural to agree with two subjects
agrees with the first subject in the sentence
can be either singular or plural
takes a plural form when subjects are joined
questions.explanation: Bepo explained that when 'as well as', 'together with', or 'alongside' is used, the verb agrees with the main subject (the first noun), not the additional noun. So 'Ade as well as Jide comes' is grammatically correct because 'Ade' is the main subject.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: Which character in the novel is described as the school's 'comic relief' with 'biting humour'?
questions.explanation: Mr. Audu, the Fine Arts teacher, is repeatedly identified as the comic relief character. He jokes about going to Afghanistan if he got a visa and saves the MD's embarrassment after the grammar controversy.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: In The Lekki Headmaster, the 'Point of No Return' referenced in Chapter 11 alludes primarily to _____.
options: the farewell ceremony at Stardom Schools
a historical slave-trade site in Badagry
questions.explanation: The 'Point of No Return' is a famous historical slave-trade site in Badagry, Lagos State, from which enslaved Africans were shipped abroad. The novel uses it as a metaphor comparing voluntary modern migration ('Japa') to historical forced migration.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.question: The farewell gift Bepo received from the Managing Director of Stardom Schools was _____.
